sentences.zh: 【唐紀五十一】起閼逢閹茂六月，盡上章執徐，凡六年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 51] Beginning from the sixth month of the year jianmao in the cycle yanmao, through shangzhang zhixu; altogether a little over six years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 51], from the sixth month of the jianmao year in the yanmao cycle through shangzhang zhixu—altogether a little more than six years.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十貞元十年（

translations.literal: Divine Martial and Sagacious Literary Emperor Dezong 10, tenth year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, tenth year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 甲戌，公元七九四年）

translations.literal: jiaxu, corresponding to AD 794)
translations.idiomatic: jiaxu, AD 794)

sentences.zh: 六月，壬寅朔，昭義節度使李抱真薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day renyin of the month, Zhaoyi Military Commissioner Li Baozhen died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the first day (renyin) of the month, Li Baozhen, military commissioner of Zhaoyi, died.

sentences.zh: 其子殿中侍御史緘與抱真從甥元仲經謀，秘不發喪，詐為抱真表，求以職事授緘。

translations.literal: His son, Palace Attendant of the Palace Secretariat Li Jian, plotted with Baozhen's nephew by marriage Yuan Zhongjing to keep the death secret and not announce mourning. They forged a memorial in Baozhen's name requesting that Jian be given his duties.
translations.idiomatic: His son Li Jian, a palace attendant in the Secretariat, conspired with Baozhen's nephew by marriage Yuan Zhongjing to conceal the death and withhold mourning. They forged a memorial in Baozhen's name asking that Jian be entrusted with his father's post.

sentences.zh: 又詐為其父書，遣裨將陳榮詣王武俊假貨財。

translations.literal: They also forged a letter in his father's name and sent the adjutant Chen Rong to Wang Wujun to borrow goods and funds.
translations.idiomatic: They also forged a letter in his father's name and sent the adjutant Chen Rong to Wang Wujun to borrow money and supplies.

sentences.zh: 武俊怒曰：「吾與乃公厚善，欲同獎王室耳，豈與汝同惡邪！

translations.literal: Wujun said in anger: "I was on excellent terms with your father and wished only to work together to support the royal house—how could I join you in evil!
translations.idiomatic: Wujun said angrily, "Your father and I were close, and we meant to support the throne together—why would I join you in villainy!

sentences.zh: 聞乃公已亡，乃敢不俟朝命而自立，又敢告我，況有求也！」

translations.literal: I hear your father is already dead, yet you dare to install yourself without awaiting the court's command—and you dare inform me of it, let alone make a request!"
translations.idiomatic: I hear your father is dead, yet you dare seize power without the court's order—and you dare come to me with this, much less ask for a loan!"

sentences.zh: 使榮歸，寄聲質責緘。

translations.literal: He sent Rong back with a message rebuking Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Rong back with a message of rebuke for Jian.

sentences.zh: 昭義步軍都虞候王延貴，汝州梁人也，素以義勇聞。

translations.literal: Wang Yangui, chief controller of the Zhaoyi infantry, was a native of Liang in Ruzhou and was long known for righteousness and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yangui, chief controller of the Zhaoyi infantry, was from Liang in Ruzhou and had long been known for courage and integrity.

sentences.zh: 上知抱真已薨，遣中使第五守進往觀變，且以軍事委王延貴。

translations.literal: The emperor, knowing that Baozhen had died, sent the palace envoy Diwu Shoujin to observe developments and entrusted military affairs to Wang Yangui.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Baozhen had died, the emperor sent the palace envoy Diwu Shoujin to assess the situation and entrusted military command to Wang Yangui.

sentences.zh: 守進至上黨，緘稱抱真有疾不能見。

translations.literal: When Shoujin reached Shangdang, Jian claimed that Baozhen was ill and could not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shoujin reached Shangdang, Jian claimed Baozhen was too ill to see him.

sentences.zh: 三日，緘乃嚴兵詣守進，守進謂之曰：「朝廷已知相公捐館，令王延貴權知軍事。

translations.literal: After three days Jian came to Shoujin with troops in battle order. Shoujin said to him: "The court already knows that the lord has passed away and has ordered Wang Yangui to act as temporary commander of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Jian came to Shoujin under arms. Shoujin told him, "The court already knows your father has died and has ordered Wang Yangui to take temporary command of the army.

sentences.zh: 侍御宜發喪行服。」

translations.literal: The Attendant should announce mourning and observe the rites of bereavement."
translations.idiomatic: You, Attendant, should announce the mourning and observe the funeral rites."

sentences.zh: 緘愕然，出，謂諸將曰：「朝廷不許緘掌事，諸君意如何？」

translations.literal: Jian was startled. He went out and said to the generals: "The court will not allow Jian to hold command—what do you gentlemen think?"
translations.idiomatic: Jian was stunned. He went out and asked the generals, "The court will not let me take command—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 莫對。

translations.literal: No one answered.
translations.idiomatic: No one replied.

sentences.zh: 緘懼，乃歸發喪，以使印及管鑰授監軍。

translations.literal: Jian, in fear, then returned to announce mourning and handed the commissioner’s seal and the keys of administration to the army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, Jian went back to announce the mourning and surrendered the commissioner’s seal and the keys of office to the army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 守進召延貴，宣口詔令視事，趣緘赴東都。

translations.literal: Shoujin summoned Yangui, proclaimed the oral edict ordering him to take charge of affairs, and urged Jian to proceed to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shoujin summoned Yangui, proclaimed the oral edict appointing him to office, and ordered Jian to go to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 元仲經出走，延貴悉歸罪於仲經，捕斬之。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhongjing fled. Yangui laid all blame on Zhongjing, seized him, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhongjing fled. Yangui blamed everything on Zhongjing, captured him, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 詔以延貴權知昭義軍事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yangui acting commander of Zhaoyi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Yangui acting commander of Zhaoyi military affairs.

sentences.zh: 雲南王異牟尋遣其弟湊羅楝獻地圖、土貢及吐蕃所給金印，請復號南詔。

translations.literal: King Yimouxun of Yunnan sent his younger brother Cuoluoleng to present a map, local tribute, and the gold seal given by the Tibetans, requesting restoration of the title Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: King Yimouxun of Yunnan sent his younger brother Cuoluoleng with a map, local tribute, and the gold seal the Tibetans had given him, asking to resume the name Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以祠部郎中袁滋為冊南詔使，賜銀窠金印，文曰：「貞元冊南詔印」。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Yuan Zi, a director in the Ministry of Rites, was made envoy to invest Nanzhao and was granted a silver-nest gold seal inscribed "Seal for Investing Nanzhao in the Zhenyuan Era."
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Yuan Zi of the Ministry of Rites was appointed envoy to invest Nanzhao and was given a silver-inlaid gold seal reading "Seal for Investing Nanzhao in the Zhenyuan Era."

sentences.zh: 滋至其國，異牟尋北面跪受冊印，稽首再拜，因與使者宴，出玄宗所賜銀平脫馬頭盤二以示滋。

translations.literal: When Zi reached his kingdom, Yimouxun faced north, knelt, and received the investiture seal. He bowed to the ground twice, then feasted with the envoy and produced two horse-head platters of silver repoussé that Emperor Xuanzong had bestowed, to show Zi.
translations.idiomatic: When Zi arrived, Yimouxun faced north, knelt, and received the investiture seal, then kowtowed twice. At the banquet with the envoy he brought out two silver repoussé horse-head platters that Emperor Xuanzong had once given him, to show Zi.

sentences.zh: 又指老笛工、歌女曰：「皇帝所賜《龜茲樂》，唯二人在耳。」

translations.literal: He also pointed to an old flute player and a songstress and said: "Of the Kuchean music the emperor bestowed, only these two remain."
translations.idiomatic: He also pointed to an old flute player and a songstress and said, "Of the Kuchean music the emperor gave us, only these two are left."

sentences.zh: 滋曰：「南詔當深思祖考，子子孫孫盡忠於唐。」

translations.literal: Zi said: "Nanzhao should deeply reflect on its ancestors and be loyal to Tang generation after generation."
translations.idiomatic: Zi said, "Nanzhao should honor its forebears and remain loyal to Tang for generations to come."

sentences.zh: 異牟尋拜曰：「敢不謹承使者之命！」

translations.literal: Yimouxun bowed and said: "How would I dare not respectfully accept the envoy's command!"
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun bowed and said, "I shall respectfully obey the envoy's charge!"

sentences.zh: 賜義武節度使張升雲名茂昭。

translations.literal: The Yiwu Military Commissioner Zhang Shengyun was granted the name Maozhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shengyun, military commissioner of Yiwu, was granted the name Maozhao.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞穆贊按度支吏贓罪，裴延齡欲出之，贊不從。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Mu Zan investigated embezzlement by an official of the Department of Public Revenue. Pei Yanling wished to release him; Zan would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Mu Zan investigated embezzlement by a revenue official. Pei Yanling wanted the man released; Zan refused.

sentences.zh: 延齡譖之，貶饒州別駕，朝士畏延齡側目。

translations.literal: Yanling slandered him, and he was demoted to vice prefect of Raozhou. Court officials feared Yanling and watched him with sidelong glances.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling slandered him, and he was demoted to vice prefect of Raozhou. Officials at court feared Yanling and dared not meet his eye.

sentences.zh: 贊，寧之子也。

translations.literal: Zan was the son of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Zan was the son of Mu Ning.

sentences.zh: 韋皋奏破吐蕃於峨和城。

translations.literal: Wei Gao reported defeating the Tibetans at Ehe Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao reported a victory over the Tibetans at Ehe Fortress.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬申朔，以王延貴為昭義留後，賜名虔休。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day renshen of the month, Wang Yangui was made acting commissioner of Zhaoyi and granted the name Qianxiu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day (renshen), Wang Yangui was appointed acting commissioner of Zhaoyi and given the name Qianxiu.

sentences.zh: 昭義行軍司馬、攝洺州刺史元誼聞虔休為留後，意不平，表請在以磁、邢、洺別為一鎮。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi, campaigning army marshal of Zhaoyi and acting prefect of Mingzhou, heard that Qianxiu had become acting commissioner. Displeased, he memorialized requesting that Ci, Xing, and Ming be made a separate command.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi, Zhaoyi's campaigning army marshal and acting prefect of Mingzhou, was displeased when Qianxiu became acting commissioner and memorialized asking that Ci, Xing, and Ming be formed into a separate command.

sentences.zh: 昭義精兵多在山東，誼厚賚以悅之。

translations.literal: Many of Zhaoyi's elite troops were in Shandong. Yi lavished rewards on them to win their favor.
translations.idiomatic: Many of Zhaoyi's best troops were in Shandong; Yi lavished gifts on them to win them over.

sentences.zh: 上屢遣中使諭之，不從。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly sent palace envoys to instruct him, but he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly sent palace envoys to reason with him, but he refused to comply.

sentences.zh: 臨洺守將夏侯仲宣以城歸虔休，虔休遣磁州刺史馬正卿督裨將石定蕃等將兵五千擊洺州。

translations.literal: Xiahou Zhongxuan, defender of Linming, surrendered the city to Qianxiu. Qianxiu sent the prefect of Cizhou Ma Zhengqing to supervise the adjutants Shi Dingfan and others in leading five thousand troops to attack Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Zhongxuan, the defender of Linming, surrendered the city to Qianxiu. Qianxiu sent Ma Zhengqing, prefect of Cizhou, with the adjutant Shi Dingfan and others at the head of five thousand men to attack Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 定蕃帥其眾二千叛歸誼，正卿退還。

translations.literal: Dingfan led two thousand of his men in revolt back to Yi; Zhengqing withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Dingfan took two thousand men and defected to Yi; Zhengqing retreated.

sentences.zh: 詔以誼為饒州刺史，誼不行。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yi prefect of Raozhou, but Yi would not go.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Yi prefect of Raozhou, but he refused to leave.

sentences.zh: 虔休自將兵攻之，引洺水以灌城。

translations.literal: Qianxiu personally led troops to attack him and diverted the Ming River to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiu led the attack in person and diverted the Ming River to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 黃少卿陷欽、橫、潯、貴等州，攻孫公器於邕州。

translations.literal: Huang Shaoqing captured Qin, Heng, Xun, Gui, and other prefectures and attacked Sun Gongqi at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shaoqing seized Qin, Heng, Xun, Gui, and other prefectures and attacked Sun Gongqi at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 九月，王虔休破元誼兵，進拔雞澤。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wang Qianxiu defeated Yuan Yi's army and advanced to take Jize.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Qianxiu defeated Yuan Yi's forces and took Jize.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡奏管官吏太多，自今缺員請且勿補，收其俸以實府庫。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling memorialized that there were too many officials under his jurisdiction. From now on, when posts fell vacant he asked that they not be filled and that their salaries be collected to replenish the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling memorialized that his department had too many officials. He asked that vacancies no longer be filled and that the salaries be kept to fill the treasury.

sentences.zh: 上欲修神龍寺，須五十尺松，不可得。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to repair Shenlong Temple and needed fifty-foot pines, but none could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to repair Shenlong Temple and needed fifty-foot pines, but none could be found.

sentences.zh: 延齡曰：「臣近見同州一谷，木數千株，皆可八十尺。」

translations.literal: Yanling said: "Your servant recently saw a valley in Tongzhou with several thousand trees, all able to reach eighty feet."
translations.idiomatic: Yanling said, "I recently saw a valley in Tongzhou with several thousand trees, every one eighty feet tall."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「開元、天寶間求美材於近畿猶不可得，今安得有之？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras fine timber could not be obtained even in the near capital districts—how could it exist now?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "In the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras you could not find fine timber even near the capital—how could such trees exist now?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天生珍材，固待聖君乃出，開元、天寶何從得之！」

translations.literal: He replied: "Heaven-born precious timber naturally waits for a sage ruler before it appears—how could the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras have obtained it!"
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Rare timber appears only for a sage ruler—how could Kaiyuan and Tianbao have had it!"

sentences.zh: 延齡奏：「左藏庫司多有失落，近因檢閱使置簿書，乃於糞土之中得銀十三萬兩，其匹段雜貨百萬有餘。

translations.literal: Yanling memorialized: "The Left Treasury office had many losses. Recently, because the reviewing commissioner set up ledgers, one hundred thirty thousand taels of silver were found in the dung and soil, and more than a million in bolts of cloth and miscellaneous goods.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling reported, "The Left Treasury had many losses. A recent audit turned up one hundred thirty thousand taels of silver in the refuse, plus more than a million in cloth and miscellaneous goods.

sentences.zh: 此皆已棄之物，即是羨餘，悉應移入雜庫以供別敕支用。」

translations.literal: These were all already discarded items and therefore counted as surplus; all should be moved into the miscellaneous treasury for disbursement by separate edict."
translations.idiomatic: These were all discarded goods and therefore surplus; they should all go into the miscellaneous treasury for special disbursements."

sentences.zh: 太府少卿韋少華不伏，抗表稱：「此皆每月申奏見在之物，請加推驗。」

translations.literal: Wei Shaohua, vice director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, would not submit. He submitted a defiant memorial saying: "These are all items reported each month as presently on hand—please conduct further investigation."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shaohua, vice director of the Imperial Treasury, protested in a memorial: "These are items reported every month as on hand—please investigate further."

sentences.zh: 執政請令三司詳覆。

translations.literal: The chief ministers asked that the three offices conduct a detailed review.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers asked the three offices to review the matter in detail.

sentences.zh: 上不許，亦不罪少華。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it and also did not punish Shaohua.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and did not punish Shaohua.

sentences.zh: 延齡每奏對，恣為詭譎，皆眾所不敢言，亦未嘗聞者，延齡處之不疑。

translations.literal: Whenever Yanling answered at audience he freely uttered deceptions that everyone else dared not speak and that had never been heard; Yanling delivered them without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yanling spoke at audience he told brazen lies no one else would dare utter; he did so without a flicker of doubt.

sentences.zh: 上亦頗知其誕妄，但以其好詆毀人，冀聞外事，故親厚之。

translations.literal: The emperor also knew fairly well that he was absurd and false, but because he liked to slander people the emperor hoped to hear news from outside and therefore treated him with favor and closeness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor knew Yanling was a liar, but because he delighted in slandering others the emperor hoped to hear outside news through him and therefore kept him close.

sentences.zh: 群臣畏延齡有寵，莫敢言，惟鹽鐵轉運使張滂、京兆尹李充、司農卿李銛以職事相關，時證其妄，而陸贄獨以身當之，日陳其不可用。

translations.literal: The ministers feared Yanling's favor and none dared speak. Only the Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Zhang Pang, the metropolitan governor Li Chong, and the minister of agriculture Li Qian, because their duties were related, sometimes proved his falsehoods; Lu Zhi alone took the risk upon himself and daily stated that he was unfit for use.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers feared Yanling's favor and kept silent. Only Zhang Pang, Li Chong, and Li Qian, whose duties overlapped his, sometimes exposed his lies; Lu Zhi alone stood in the breach and argued daily that he must not be used.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬申，贄上書極陳延齡奸詐，數其罪惡，其略曰：「延齡以聚斂為長策，以詭妄為嘉謀，以掊克斂怨為匪躬，以靖譖服讒為盡節，總典籍之所惡以為智術，冒聖哲之所戒以為行能，可謂堯代之共工，魯邦之少卯也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day renshen, Zhi submitted a memorial vehemently exposing Yanling's treachery and fraud and enumerating his crimes. In summary it said: "Yanling takes extortion as his chief policy, deceit and falsehood as excellent counsel, squeezing the people and gathering hatred as devotion to the ruler, and quieting slander and submitting to calumny as full loyalty. He gathers everything the classics condemn as wisdom and dares everything the sages warn against as ability. He may be called the Gong Gong of the age of Yao and the Shao Mao of the state of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renshen, Zhi submitted a memorial denouncing Yanling's treachery and listing his crimes. In part it read: "Yanling treats extortion as statecraft, deceit as good counsel, squeezing the people as loyalty, and silencing slander as devotion. He makes a virtue of everything the classics condemn and dares everything the sages forbid. He is a Gong Gong for our age and a Shao Mao for our court.

sentences.zh: 跡其奸蠹，日長月滋，陰秘者固未盡彰，敗露者尤難悉數。」

translations.literal: Tracing his treachery and corruption, it grows day by day and month by month. What remains hidden has certainly not all been revealed; what has been exposed is especially hard to count in full."
translations.idiomatic: His corruption grows daily; what remains hidden is not yet fully known, and what has been exposed is already beyond numbering."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下若意其負謗，則誠宜亟為辨明。

translations.literal: It also said: "If Your Majesty thinks he has been wronged by slander, you should indeed clarify the matter at once.
translations.idiomatic: It also said, "If Your Majesty believes he has been slandered, you should clear his name at once.

sentences.zh: 陛下若知其無良，又安可曲加容掩！」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty knows he is without goodness, how can you bend to cover and shield him!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty knows he is worthless, how can you bend to protect him!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「陛下姑欲保持，曾無詰問，延齡謂能蔽惑，不復懼思。

translations.literal: It also said: "Your Majesty for the time being wishes to keep him and has never questioned him. Yanling believes he can blind and delude you and no longer fears or reflects.
translations.idiomatic: It also said, "Your Majesty has kept him on without inquiry. Yanling thinks he has blinded you and no longer fears consequences.

sentences.zh: 移東就西，便為課績，取此適彼，遂號羨餘，愚弄朝廷，有同兒戲。」

translations.literal: Shifting from east to west counts as fulfilling quotas; taking from here to suit there is then called surplus. He fools the court as if it were child's play."
translations.idiomatic: Moving funds from one account to another counts as meeting targets; shifting assets from place to place he calls surplus. He toys with the court like a child at play."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「矯詭之能，誣罔之辭，遇事輒行，應口便發，靡日不有，靡時不為，又難以備陳也。」

translations.literal: It also said: "His power to twist and deceive, his words to mislead and hoodwink—whenever a matter arises he acts at once, and whatever is asked he answers on the spot. There is no day without it and no hour without it; it is again hard to set forth in full."
translations.idiomatic: It also said, "His deceits and lies come at every turn—there is no day or hour without them—and they are too many to list."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「昔趙高指鹿為馬，臣謂鹿之與馬，物類猶同，豈若延齡掩有為無，指無為有。」

translations.literal: It also said: "In former times Zhao Gao called a deer a horse. Your servant considers that deer and horse are still of the same kind of thing—how can that compare with Yanling, who hides what exists as if it did not and points to what does not exist as if it did?"
translations.idiomatic: It also said, "Zhao Gao once called a deer a horse—but deer and horse are at least alike. Yanling hides what exists and invents what does not."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「延齡凶妄，流布寰區，上自公卿近臣，下逮輿台賤品，喧喧談議，億萬為徒，能以上言，其人有幾！

translations.literal: It also said: "Yanling is vicious and reckless; his reputation spreads throughout the realm. From high ministers and close attendants down to carriage men and humble ranks, the noisy talk and discussion—tens of millions follow him. Those who can speak up to the throne—how many are there!
translations.idiomatic: It also said, "Yanling's villainy is known everywhere, from ministers down to common servants—millions talk of it. Yet how many dare speak to the throne!

sentences.zh: 臣以卑鄙，任當台衡，情激於衷，雖欲罷而不能自默也。」

translations.literal: Your servant, though base, holds the post that should balance the scales. My feelings are stirred within; though I wish to stop, I cannot keep silent."
translations.idiomatic: Though I am unworthy, I hold the highest office. My heart compels me—though I wish to hold my tongue, I cannot."

sentences.zh: 書奏，上不悅，待延齡益厚。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted the emperor was displeased and treated Yanling all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived the emperor was displeased and treated Yanling even more favorably.

sentences.zh: 十二月，王虔休乘冰合度壕，急攻洺州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Wang Qianxiu, taking advantage of frozen moats, crossed the ditches and pressed the attack on Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Wang Qianxiu crossed the frozen moats and launched a fierce assault on Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元誼出兵擊之，虔休不勝而返，日暮冰解，士卒死者太半。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi led troops out to strike him. Qianxiu did not prevail and withdrew. At dusk the ice broke up and more than half the soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi counterattacked. Qianxiu was beaten back, and at dusk the ice gave way—more than half his men perished.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事陸贄以上知待之厚，事有不可，常力爭之。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow Grand Councillor, knew that the emperor treated him generously. When something was not right he often strove against it with all his force.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, vice director of the Secretariat and fellow grand councillor, knew the emperor favored him; whenever he saw something wrong he argued fiercely.

sentences.zh: 所親或規其太銳，贄曰：「吾上不負天子，下不負所學，他無所恤。」

translations.literal: Those close to him sometimes admonished him that he was too sharp. Zhi said: "Above I do not fail the Son of Heaven; below I do not fail what I have learned—beyond that I have no concern."
translations.idiomatic: Friends sometimes warned him he was too blunt. Zhi said, "I owe the emperor my loyalty above and my principles below—nothing else concerns me."

sentences.zh: 裴延齡日短贄於上。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling daily spoke ill of Zhi to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling daily slandered Zhi to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 趙憬之入相也，贄實引之，既而有憾於贄，密以贄所譏彈延齡事告延齡，故延齡益得以為計，上由是信延齡而不直贄。

translations.literal: When Zhao Jing entered the chancellorship, Zhi had in fact recommended him. Later he bore resentment toward Zhi and secretly told Yanling what Zhi had criticized and impeached Yanling for. Thus Yanling was all the more able to plot, and the emperor thereby trusted Yanling and did not side with Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jing had entered the chancellorship on Zhi's recommendation, but later resented him and secretly told Yanling what Zhi had said against him. Yanling used this to his advantage, and the emperor came to trust Yanling and doubt Zhi.

sentences.zh: 贄與憬約至上前極論延齡奸邪，上怒形於色，憬默而無言。

translations.literal: Zhi and Jing agreed to argue vehemently before the throne about Yanling's treachery and wickedness. The emperor's anger showed on his face; Jing was silent and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Jing had agreed to argue Yanling's guilt before the emperor. The emperor's anger showed on his face; Jing said nothing.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，贄罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Zhi was removed and made guest of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Zhi was dismissed and made tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，勃海文王欽茂卒，子宏臨早死，族弟元義立。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wén King Qinmao of Bohai died. His son Honglin had died young, and a clansman younger cousin Yuan Yi was installed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Literary King Qinmao of Bohai died. His son Honglin had died young, and a younger clansman, Yuan Yi, took the throne.

sentences.zh: 元義猜虐，國人殺之，立宏臨之子華嶼，是為成王，改元中興。

translations.literal: Yuan Yi was suspicious and cruel; the people killed him and installed Honglin's son Huayu, who became King Cheng and changed the era name to Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yi was cruel and suspicious; the people killed him and set up Honglin's son Huayu as King Cheng, changing the era name to Zhongxing.

sentences.zh: 華嶼卒，復立欽茂少子嵩鄰，是為康王，改元正歷。

translations.literal: When Huayu died, Qinmao's youngest son Songlin was again installed; he became King Kang and changed the era name to Zhengli.
translations.idiomatic: When Huayu died, Qinmao's youngest son Songlin became King Kang and changed the era name to Zhengli.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十貞元十一年（

translations.literal: Divine Martial and Sagacious Literary Emperor Dezong 10, eleventh year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, eleventh year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 乙亥，公元七九五年）

translations.literal: yihai, corresponding to AD 795)
translations.idiomatic: yihai, AD 795)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，乙巳，冊拜嵩鄰為忽汗州都督、勃海王。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on the day yisi, Songlin was invested and appointed military commissioner of Hohan Prefecture and king of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on yisi, Songlin was invested as military commissioner of Hohan Prefecture and king of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 陸贄既罷相，裴延齡因譖京兆尹李充、衛尉卿張滂、前司農卿李銛黨於贄。

translations.literal: After Lu Zhi had been removed from the chancellorship, Pei Yanling slandered the metropolitan governor Li Chong, the minister of the guard Zhang Pang, and the former minister of agriculture Li Qian as partisans of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Zhi left office, Pei Yanling accused the metropolitan governor Li Chong, Minister of the Guard Zhang Pang, and former Minister of Agriculture Li Qian of being Zhi's partisans.

sentences.zh: 會早，延齡奏言：「贄等失勢怨望，言於眾曰，『天下旱，百姓且流亡，度支多欠諸軍芻糧，軍中人馬無所食，其事奈何！』

translations.literal: There happened to be drought. Yanling memorialized: "Zhi and the others, having lost power, are resentful. They say among the people: 'The realm is in drought; the common people are about to flee. The Department of Public Revenue owes much fodder and grain to the armies; men and horses in the armies have nothing to eat—what is to be done about this!
translations.idiomatic: There was a drought. Yanling reported, "Zhi and his allies, bitter over their fall, are telling people, 'The land is dry, the people will flee, the revenue office owes the armies fodder and grain, and the troops have nothing to feed their horses—what will become of us!

sentences.zh: 以動搖眾心，其意非止欲中傷臣而已。」

translations.literal: —to shake the hearts of the multitude. Their intent is not merely to strike at your servant."
translations.idiomatic: —to shake public confidence. Their aim is not merely to harm me."

sentences.zh: 後數日，上獵苑中，適有神策軍士訴云：「度支不給馬芻。」

translations.literal: Several days later the emperor was hunting in the park when a Shence Army soldier happened to complain, saying: "The Department of Public Revenue does not supply horse fodder."
translations.idiomatic: Days later, while hunting in the park, a Shence soldier complained that the revenue office was not supplying horse fodder."

sentences.zh: 上意延齡言為信，遽還宮。

translations.literal: The emperor took Yanling's words as true and hurried back to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed Yanling and hurried back to the palace.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，壬戌，貶贄為忠州別駕，充為涪州長史，滂為汀州長史，銛為邵州長史。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day renxu, Zhi was demoted to vice prefect of Zhongzhou, Chong to chief administrator of Fuzhou, Pang to chief administrator of Tingzhou, and Qian to chief administrator of Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on renxu, Zhi was demoted to vice prefect of Zhongzhou, Chong to chief administrator of Fuzhou, Pang to Tingzhou, and Qian to Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 初，陽城自處士征為諫議大夫，拜官不辭。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yang Cheng was summoned from private life to be Censor-in-Chief. He accepted the appointment without declining.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yang Cheng was summoned from private life to be supervising censor and accepted without demur.

sentences.zh: 未至京師，人皆想望風采，曰：「城必諫諍，死職下。」

translations.literal: Before he reached the capital everyone looked to his bearing and said: "Cheng is sure to remonstrate and die in his post."
translations.idiomatic: Before he reached the capital everyone expected great things of him and said, "Cheng will remonstrate unto death."

sentences.zh: 及至，諸諫官紛紛言事細碎，天子益厭苦之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the various remonstrating officials all spoke on trifling matters in detail, and the Son of Heaven grew all the more weary and vexed.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the other remonstrating officials pestered the throne with petty complaints, and the emperor grew only more weary.

sentences.zh: 而城方與二弟及客日夜痛飲，人莫能窺其際，皆以為虛得名耳。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Cheng was drinking heavily day and night with his two younger brothers and guests. No one could fathom his intentions; all thought he had only an empty reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Cheng drank day and night with his two brothers and guests. No one could fathom him; all thought his reputation hollow.

sentences.zh: 前進士河南韓愈作《爭臣論》以譏之，城亦不以屑意。

translations.literal: The former presented scholar Han Yu of Henan wrote "On Remonstrating Ministers" to mock him; Cheng also did not regard it with concern.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu of Henan, a former presented scholar, wrote "On Remonstrating Ministers" to mock him; Cheng paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 有欲造城而問者，城揣知其意，輒強與酒。

translations.literal: When someone wished to visit Cheng to question him, Cheng guessed his intent and would force wine on him.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone came to question him, Cheng guessed their purpose and forced wine on them.

sentences.zh: 客或時先醉僕席上，城或時先醉臥客懷中，不能聽客語。

translations.literal: Sometimes the guest would first grow drunk and collapse on the mat; sometimes Cheng would first grow drunk and lie in the guest's embrace, unable to hear the guest's words.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the guest passed out first on the mat; sometimes Cheng passed out in the guest's arms, too drunk to listen.

sentences.zh: 及陸贄等坐貶，上怒未解，中外惴恐，以為罪且不測，無敢救者。

translations.literal: When Lu Zhi and the others were punished by demotion, the emperor's anger had not yet subsided. Inside and outside the court all were fearful, thinking the crime might be beyond measure, and no one dared rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Zhi and the others were demoted, the emperor's anger had not cooled. Court and country were afraid the punishment might go further, and no one dared intervene.

sentences.zh: 城聞而起曰：「不可令天子信用奸臣，殺無罪人。」

translations.literal: Cheng heard of it and rose, saying: "We cannot let the Son of Heaven trust treacherous ministers and kill the guiltless."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng heard and rose, saying, "We cannot let the emperor trust villains and kill innocent men."

sentences.zh: 即帥拾遺王仲舒、歸登、右補闕熊執易、崔邠等守延英門，上疏論延齡奸佞，贄等無罪。

translations.literal: He immediately led the remonstrance officials Wang Zhongshu and Gui Deng and the right supplementer Xiong Zhiyi, Cui Bin, and others to hold the Yanying Gate, submitting a memorial arguing that Yanling was treacherous and fawning and that Zhi and the others were guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: He led the remonstrance officials Wang Zhongshu, Gui Deng, Xiong Zhiyi, Cui Bin, and others to block the Yanying Gate and memorialized that Yanling was corrupt and that Zhi and his allies were innocent.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，欲加城等罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and wished to impose punishment on Cheng and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and meant to punish Cheng and the others.

sentences.zh: 太子為之營救，上意乃解，令宰相諭遣之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent interceded for them; the emperor's mind was then eased and he ordered the chief ministers to instruct and send them away.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent interceded; the emperor relented and ordered the chancellors to send them away with an explanation.

sentences.zh: 於是金吾將軍張萬福聞諫官伏閣諫，趨往至延英門，大言賀曰：「朝廷有直臣，天下必太平矣！」

translations.literal: Thereupon Jinwu General Zhang Wanfu, hearing that the remonstrating officials were remonstrating at the gate, hurried to the Yanying Gate and cried out in congratulation: "The court has upright ministers—the realm is sure to be at peace!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinwu General Zhang Wanfu, hearing the censors were remonstrating at the gate, ran to the Yanying Gate and shouted in joy, "The court has upright ministers—the realm will be at peace!"

sentences.zh: 遂遍拜城與仲舒等，已而連呼「太平萬歲！

translations.literal: He then bowed to Cheng and Zhongshu and the others in turn, and soon cried out again, "Long live the peace!
translations.idiomatic: He bowed to Cheng, Zhongshu, and the others in turn, then shouted again, "Long live peace!

sentences.zh: 太平萬歲！」

translations.literal: Long live the peace!"
translations.idiomatic: Long live peace!"

sentences.zh: 萬福，武人，年八十餘，自此名重天下。

translations.literal: Wanfu was a military man, over eighty years old; from this his name was weighty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wanfu was a soldier, over eighty; from this his fame spread across the realm.

sentences.zh: 登，崇敬之子也。

translations.literal: Deng was the son of Chongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Gui Deng was the son of Chongjing.

sentences.zh: 時朝夕相延齡，陽城曰：「脫以延齡為相，城當取白麻壞之，慟哭於庭。」

translations.literal: At the time they daily kept company with Yanling. Yang Cheng said: "If by chance Yanling is made chancellor, Cheng will take the white hemp edict and destroy it, weeping and wailing in the courtyard."
translations.idiomatic: Yanling was at court daily. Yang Cheng said, "If Yanling is made chancellor, I will tear up the appointment edict and wail in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 有李繁者，泌之子也，城盡疏延齡過惡，欲密論之，以繁故人子，使之繕寫，繁徑以告延齡。

translations.literal: There was one Li Fan, son of Li Bi; Cheng set forth all Yanling's faults and wished to discuss them secretly. Because Fan was the son of an old friend, he had him copy it; Fan went straight and told Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan, son of Li Bi, copied a memorial in which Cheng listed Yanling's crimes for secret presentation; Fan took it straight to Yanling.

sentences.zh: 延齡先詣上，一一自解。

translations.literal: Yanling went first to the emperor and explained each point himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yanling went to the emperor first and answered each charge himself.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上以為妄，不之省。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor thought it false and did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor dismissed it as fabrication and took no notice.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，幽州奏破奚王啜利等六萬餘眾。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Youzhou reported defeating the Xi king Zhuoli and others, more than sixty thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Youzhou reported defeating the Xi king Zhuoli and more than sixty thousand of his followers.

sentences.zh: 回鶻奉誠可汗卒，無子，國人立其相骨咄祿為可汗。

translations.literal: The Uyghur Fengcheng Khagan died without a son; the people installed his chancellor Kutlug as khagan.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghur Fengcheng Khagan died childless; the people made his chancellor Kutlug khagan.

sentences.zh: 骨咄祿本姓□夾跌氏，辯慧有勇略，自天親時典兵馬用事，大臣諸酋長皆畏服之。

translations.literal: Kutlug was originally of the Ashina clan by surname. He was eloquent and brave, and from the time of Khagan Tianqin had controlled the armies and held power; great ministers and all tribal chiefs feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Kutlug was originally of the Ashina clan. Clever and bold, he had commanded troops since Khagan Tianqin's day; ministers and chiefs alike feared him.

sentences.zh: 既為可汗，冒姓藥葛羅氏，遣使來告喪。

translations.literal: Once he became khagan, he took the surname Yaghlakar and sent envoys to announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: As khagan he took the surname Yaghlakar and sent envoys to announce the death.

sentences.zh: 自天親可汗以上子孫幼稚者，皆內之闕庭。

translations.literal: All descendants of khagans from Tianqin upward who were still young were brought inside the palace precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Young descendants of khagans from Tianqin upward were all brought into the court.

sentences.zh: 五月，丁丑，以宣武留後李萬榮、昭義左司馬領留後王虔休皆為節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day dingchou, Li Wanrong, acting commissioner of Xuanwu, and Wang Qianxiu, left army marshal acting as commissioner of Zhaoyi, were both made military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou in the fifth month, Li Wanrong of Xuanwu and Wang Qianxiu of Zhaoyi were both appointed military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 甲申，河東節度使李自良薨。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, Hedong Military Commissioner Li Ziliang died.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Li Ziliang, military commissioner of Hedong, died.

sentences.zh: 戊子，監軍王定遠奏請以行軍司馬李說為留後。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, Army Supervisor Wang Dingyuan memorialized requesting that campaigning army marshal Li Shuo be made acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, army supervisor Wang Dingyuan asked that campaigning army marshal Li Shuo be made acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 說，神通之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Shuo was a fifth-generation descendant of Li Shentong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shuo was a fifth-generation descendant of Li Shentong.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，遣秘書監張薦冊拜回鶻可汗骨咄祿為騰裡邏羽錄沒密施合胡祿毘伽懷信可汗。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, Secretariat Director Zhang Jian was sent to invest the Uyghur Khagan Kutlug as Tengri Bogu Ulug Moch Baghla Kül Bilge Khaiduk Khagan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Zhang Jian was sent to invest Kutlug as Tengri Bogu Ulug Moch Baghla Kül Bilge Khaiduk Khagan.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，以李說為河東留後，知府事。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Li Shuo was made acting commissioner of Hedong and directed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Li Shuo was appointed acting commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 說深德王定遠，請鑄監軍印，從之。

translations.literal: Shuo was deeply grateful to Wang Dingyuan and requested that a seal for the army supervisor be cast; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was deeply obliged to Wang Dingyuan and asked that an army-supervisor seal be cast; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 監軍有印自定遠始。

translations.literal: Army supervisors having seals began with Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisors having their own seals began with Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙寅朔，陽城改國子司業，坐言裴延齡故也。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day bingyin of the month, Yang Cheng was changed to vice director of the Directorate of Education, because he had spoken against Pei Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day (bingyin), Yang Cheng was made vice director of the Directorate of Education for having denounced Pei Yanling.

sentences.zh: 王定遠自恃有功於李說，專河東軍政，易置諸將。

translations.literal: Wang Dingyuan relied on his merit toward Li Shuo and monopolized Hedong military affairs, replacing the generals at will.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dingyuan, trusting in his service to Li Shuo, dominated Hedong military affairs and replaced generals at will.

sentences.zh: 說不能盡從，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Shuo could not fully follow him; because of this there was a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo could not always comply, and a breach opened between them.

sentences.zh: 定遠以私怒拉殺大將彭令茵，埋馬矢中，將士皆憤怒。

translations.literal: Dingyuan, in private anger, seized and killed the great general Peng Lingyin and buried him in horse dung; officers and soldiers were all furious.
translations.idiomatic: In a private rage Dingyuan killed the great general Peng Lingyin and buried him in horse dung; the troops were furious.

sentences.zh: 說奏其狀，定遠聞之，直詣說，拔刀刺之。

translations.literal: Shuo reported the facts; when Dingyuan heard of it he went straight to Shuo and drew a knife to stab him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo reported the crime; Dingyuan went to him and drew a knife.

sentences.zh: 說走免。

translations.literal: Shuo fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo fled and escaped.

sentences.zh: 定遠召諸將，以箱貯敕及告身二十餘通，示之曰：「有敕，令說詣京師，以行軍司馬李景略為留後，諸君皆遷官。」

translations.literal: Dingyuan summoned the generals, took a box holding more than twenty edicts and appointment documents, showed them, and said: "There is an edict ordering Shuo to go to the capital and making campaigning army marshal Li Jinglue acting commissioner; you gentlemen are all promoted."
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan summoned the generals, produced a box of edicts and commissions, and said, "An edict sends Shuo to the capital and makes Li Jinglue acting commissioner; you are all promoted."

sentences.zh: 眾皆拜。

translations.literal: The crowd all bowed.
translations.idiomatic: All bowed.

sentences.zh: 大將馬良輔竊視箱中，皆定遠告身及所受敕也，乃麾眾曰：「敕告皆偽，不可受也。」

translations.literal: The great general Ma Liangfu stole a look in the box; they were all Dingyuan's own commissions and edicts he had received—he then waved the crowd on and said: "The edicts and announcements are all false and cannot be accepted."
translations.idiomatic: General Ma Liangfu peeked inside: they were Dingyuan's own commissions. He cried, "These orders are forged—do not obey them."

sentences.zh: 定遠走登乾陽樓，呼其麾下，莫應，逾城而墜，為枯木卉所傷而死。

translations.literal: Dingyuan fled and climbed the Qianyang Tower, calling his subordinates; none answered. He leaped over the wall and fell; he was injured on withered trees and shrubs and died.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan fled to Qianyang Tower and called his men; none came. He leapt from the wall, struck dead wood, and died.

sentences.zh: 八月，辛亥，司徒兼侍中北平莊武王馬燧薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day xinhai, Grand Mentor and Palace Attendant Ma Sui, King Zhuangwu of Beiping, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on xinhai, Ma Sui, King Zhuangwu of Beiping, died.

sentences.zh: 閏月，戊辰，元誼以洺州詐降。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day wuchen, Yuan Yi feigned surrender of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on wuchen, Yuan Yi pretended to surrender Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 王虔休遣裨將將二千人入城，誼皆殺之。

translations.literal: Wang Qianxiu sent an adjutant with two thousand men into the city; Yi killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qianxiu sent two thousand men into the city; Yi killed them all.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁巳，加韋皋雲南安撫使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day dingsi, Wei Gao was made pacification commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingsi, Wei Gao was made pacification commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 橫海節度使程懷直，不恤士卒，獵於野，數日不歸。

translations.literal: Heng-Hai Military Commissioner Cheng Huaizhi did not care for his soldiers and hunted in the wilds for many days without returning.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Huaizhi, military commissioner of Heng-Hai, neglected his troops and hunted in the countryside for days on end.

sentences.zh: 懷直從父兄懷信為兵馬使，因眾心之怨，閉門拒之，懷直奔歸京師。

translations.literal: Huaizhi's elder cousin by the father's line Huaixin was army horse commissioner; exploiting the soldiers' resentment, he shut the gates against him. Huaizhi fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Cheng Huaixin, army horse commissioner, exploited the troops' anger, shut him out, and Huaizhi fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁丑，以懷信為橫海留後。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day dingchou, Huaixin was made acting commissioner of Heng-Hai.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingchou, Huaixin was made acting commissioner of Heng-Hai.

sentences.zh: 南詔攻吐蕃昆明城，取之。

translations.literal: Nanzhao attacked the Tibetan city of Kunming and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao attacked the Tibetan city of Kunming and captured it.

sentences.zh: 又虜施、順二蠻王。

translations.literal: They also captured the kings of the Shi and Shun tribes.
translations.idiomatic: They also captured the Shi and Shun tribal kings.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十貞元十二年（

translations.literal: Divine Martial and Sagacious Literary Emperor Dezong 10, twelfth year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, twelfth year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 丙子，公元七九六年）

translations.literal: bingzi, corresponding to AD 796)
translations.idiomatic: bingzi, AD 796)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚子，元誼、石定蕃等帥洺州兵五千人及其家人萬餘口奔魏州。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day gengzi, Yuan Yi, Shi Dingfan, and others led five thousand soldiers of Mingzhou and more than ten thousand family members to flee to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on gengzi, Yuan Yi, Shi Dingfan, and others led five thousand Mingzhou troops and more than ten thousand dependents to Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上釋不問，命田緒安撫之。

translations.literal: The emperor pardoned them without inquiry and ordered Tian Xu to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pardoned them without punishment and ordered Tian Xu to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以渾瑊、王武俊並兼中書令。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Hun Jian and Wang Wujun were both made concurrent Palace Grandees Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Hun Jian and Wang Wujun were both made concurrent grandees of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 己巳，加嚴震、田緒、劉濟、韋皋並同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Yan Zhen, Tian Xu, Liu Ji, and Wei Gao were all made fellow grand councillors.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Yan Zhen, Tian Xu, Liu Ji, and Wei Gao were all made fellow grand councillors.

sentences.zh: 天下節度、觀察使，悉加檢校官以悅其意。

translations.literal: Military commissioners and observation commissioners throughout the realm were all given acting ministerial titles to please them.
translations.idiomatic: Military and observation commissioners empire-wide were given acting ministerial titles to gratify them.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲午，韋皋奏降西南蠻高萬唐等二萬餘口。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiawu, Wei Gao reported the submission of more than twenty thousand men of the southwestern barbarians, including Gao Wantang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiawu, Wei Gao reported more than twenty thousand southwestern tribesmen, including Gao Wantang, had submitted.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，以閒廄、宮苑使李齊運為禮部尚書，戶部侍郎裴延齡為戶部尚書，使職如故。

translations.literal: On the day yisi, Li Qiyun, commissioner of the imperial stud and palace parks, was made minister of rites, and Vice Minister of Revenue Pei Yanling was made minister of revenue, their commission duties unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Li Qiyun was made minister of rites and Pei Yanling minister of revenue, retaining their special duties.

sentences.zh: 齊運無才能學術，專以柔佞得幸於上，每宰相對罷，則齊運次進決其議。

translations.literal: Qiyun had no ability or learning; he won the emperor's favor solely through softness and flattery. Whenever the chief ministers finished audience, Qiyun would enter next and decide their deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Qiyun had no talent; he won favor by flattery alone. After each council session he entered and overruled the ministers' decisions.

sentences.zh: 或病臥家，上欲有所除授，往往遣中使就問之。

translations.literal: When he was ill at home, if the emperor wished to make an appointment he often sent a palace envoy to ask him at his house.
translations.idiomatic: Even when ill at home, the emperor sent palace envoys to consult him on appointments.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，韶王暹薨。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, Prince Shao of Zhao died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Prince Shao of Zhao died.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使田緒尚嘉誠公主，有庶子三人，季安最幼，公主子之，以為副大使。

translations.literal: Weibo Military Commissioner Tian Xu had married Princess Jiacheng and had three sons by a concubine; the youngest, Ji'an, was favored by the princess as her son and was made deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xu of Weibo had married Princess Jiacheng; of three sons by a concubine, the youngest Ji'an was adopted by the princess and made deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚午，緒暴薨。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengwu, Xu died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on gengwu, Xu died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 左右匿之，使季安領軍事，年十五。

translations.literal: His attendants concealed it and had Ji'an take command of the army; he was fifteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: His staff concealed the death and had fifteen-year-old Ji'an take command.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，發喪，推季安為留後。

translations.literal: On the day yihai mourning was announced and Ji'an was pushed forward as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai mourning was announced and Ji'an was made acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，上生日，故事，命沙門、道士講論於麟德殿，至是，始命以儒士參之。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, the emperor's birthday. By precedent, Buddhist and Daoist monks were ordered to discourse in Qinde Hall; from this time Confucian scholars were first ordered to take part.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, the emperor's birthday. By custom monks lectured in Qinde Hall; now Confucian scholars joined them for the first time.

sentences.zh: 四門博士韋渠牟嘲談辯給，上悅之，旬月，遷右補闕，始有寵。

translations.literal: Four-Gates academician Wei Qumou was sharp in ridicule and debate; the emperor was pleased with him. Within ten days he was promoted to right supplementer and first gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qumou of the Four Gates Academy was quick with wit; within ten days he was promoted to right supplementer and won favor.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申，邠寧節度使張獻甫暴薨，監軍楊明議請都虞候楊朝晟權知留後。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day bingshen, Binning Military Commissioner Zhang Xianfu died suddenly. Army Supervisor Yang Mingyi asked that chief controller Yang Chaocheng act as temporary commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen in the fifth month, Zhang Xianfu of Binning died suddenly; army supervisor Yang Mingyi asked that Yang Chaocheng act as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，以朝晟為邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: On the day jiachen, Chaocheng was made military commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Chaocheng was made military commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙丑，以監句當左神策竇文場、監句當右神策霍仙鳴皆為護軍中尉，監左神威軍使張尚進、監右神威軍使焦希望皆為中護軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day yichou, Dou Wenchang, supervising the Left Shence Army, and Huo Xianming, supervising the Right Shence Army, were both made chief protectors of the army; Zhang Shangjin, supervising the Left Shenwei Army, and Jiao Xiwang, supervising the Right Shenwei Army, were both made secondary protectors.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou in the sixth month, Dou Wenchang and Huo Xianming were made chief protectors of the army; Zhang Shangjin and Jiao Xiwang were made secondary protectors.

sentences.zh: 初，上置六統軍，視六尚書，以處節度使罷鎮者，相承用麻紙寫制。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had established six army commanders, ranking them with the six ministers, to place military commissioners who had left their commands; they customarily used hemp paper for the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had created six army commands, equal to the six ministries, for retired commissioners; appointments were written on hemp paper.

sentences.zh: 至是，文場諷宰相比統軍降麻。

translations.literal: At this time Wenchang hinted that the chief ministers should use white hemp for the army commanders as well.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang pressed the chancellors to use white hemp for army commanders too.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士鄭絪奏言：「故事惟封王、命相用白麻，今以命中尉，不識陛下特以寵文場邪，遂為著令也？」

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Zheng Qun memorialized: "By precedent only enfeoffing kings and appointing chancellors use white hemp. Now appointing the protectors of the army—does Your Majesty mean to favor Wenchang specially, or is this to become a fixed rule?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qun of the Hanlin Academy wrote: "Only enfeoffing princes and appointing chancellors use white hemp. Are you favoring Wenchang alone, or making this permanent?"

sentences.zh: 上乃謂文場曰：「武德、貞觀時，中人不過員外將軍同正耳，衣緋者無幾。

translations.literal: The emperor then said to Wenchang: "In the Wude and Zhenguan eras eunuchs were no more than acting outside generals of the same rank, and few wore red.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Wenchang, "Under Wude and Zhenguan, eunuchs were only acting outside generals; few wore red.

sentences.zh: 自輔國以來，墮壞制度。

translations.literal: Since Fuguo the system has been corrupted.
translations.idiomatic: Since Li Fuguo the system has rotted.

sentences.zh: 朕今用爾，不謂無私。

translations.literal: I employ you now—not that I have no private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I use you now—but not without reason.

sentences.zh: 若復以麻制宣告天下，必謂爾脅我為之矣。」

translations.literal: If I again proclaim this to the realm with a hemp appointment, they will surely say you forced me to do it."
translations.idiomatic: If I announce this with white hemp, the realm will say you forced my hand."

sentences.zh: 文場叩頭謝。

translations.literal: Wenchang kowtowed and thanked him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang kowtowed in thanks.

sentences.zh: 遂焚其麻，命並統軍自今皆中書降敕。

translations.literal: The hemp was then burned, and from this time all army commanders were to receive edicts from the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The hemp was burned; henceforth army commanders would receive Secretariat edicts.

sentences.zh: 明日，上謂絪曰：「宰相不能違拒中人，朕得卿言悟耳。」

translations.literal: The next day the emperor said to Qun: "The chief ministers cannot refuse the eunuchs—I was enlightened by your words."
translations.idiomatic: Next day the emperor told Qun, "Chancellors cannot refuse eunuchs—you opened my eyes."

sentences.zh: 是時竇、霍勢傾中外，籓鎮將帥多出神策軍、台省清要亦有出其門者矣。

translations.literal: At this time Dou and Huo dominated inside and outside; many frontier commanders and key central posts came from the Shence Army or their faction.
translations.idiomatic: Dou and Huo now dominated court and country; many generals and central posts came from their faction.

sentences.zh: 宣武節度使李萬榮病風，昏不知事，霍仙鳴薦宣武押牙劉沐可委軍政。

translations.literal: Xuanwu Military Commissioner Li Wanrong had a stroke and did not know affairs; Huo Xianming recommended Xuanwu adjutant Liu Mu as fit to entrust with military government.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wanrong of Xuanwu was paralyzed; Huo Xianming recommended adjutant Liu Mu to run the command.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以沐為行軍司馬。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Mu was made campaigning army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Mu was made campaigning army marshal.

sentences.zh: 宣歙觀察使劉贊卒。

translations.literal: Xuan-She Observation Commissioner Liu Zan died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zan, observation commissioner of Xuan-She, died.

sentences.zh: 初，上以奉天窘乏，故還宮以來，尤專意聚斂。

translations.literal: Earlier, because of the straits at Fengtian, since returning to the palace the emperor had been especially intent on amassing wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Since the hardship at Fengtian, the emperor had been obsessed with gathering wealth.

sentences.zh: 籓鎮多以進奉市恩，皆云「稅外方圓」，亦云「用度羨餘」，其實或割留常賦，或增斂百姓，或減刻吏祿，或販鬻蔬果，往往私自入，所進才什一二。

translations.literal: Many military commissioners used tribute offerings to buy favor, all saying "surplus outside the tax" or "surplus from expenses"; in fact they sometimes withheld regular levies, sometimes increased exactions on the people, sometimes cut officials' salaries, sometimes sold vegetables and fruit—often keeping the proceeds privately, so that only one or two tenths of what was presented actually arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners bought favor with "tribute": "surplus beyond tax" or "budget surplus." In truth they withheld levies, taxed the people harder, cut salaries, or sold goods privately—only a tenth reached court.

sentences.zh: 李兼在江西有月進，韋皋在西川有日進。

translations.literal: Li Jian in Jiangxi made monthly presentations; Wei Gao in Xichuan made daily presentations.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jian in Jiangxi sent monthly tribute; Wei Gao in Xichuan sent daily tribute.

sentences.zh: 其後常州刺史濟源裴肅以進奉遷浙東觀察使，刺史進奉自肅始。

translations.literal: Later Changzhou Prefect Pei Su of Jiyuan was transferred to Zhedong observation commissioner through tribute; prefects presenting tribute began with Su.
translations.idiomatic: Later Pei Su of Changzhou rose to Zhedong observer through tribute—the prefects' tribute race began with him.

sentences.zh: 及劉贊卒，判官嚴綬掌留務，竭府庫以進奉，征為刑部員外郎，幕僚進奉自綬始。

translations.literal: When Liu Zan died, judge Yan Shou handled the remaining affairs and emptied the treasury for tribute; he was summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Justice—staff tribute began with Shou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zan died, judge Yan Shou drained the treasury for tribute and was made vice director of justice—staff tribute began with Shou.

sentences.zh: 綬，蜀人也。

translations.literal: Shou was a man of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was from Shu.

sentences.zh: 李萬榮疾病，其子乃為兵馬使。

translations.literal: Li Wanrong was ill; his son then became army horse commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wanrong fell ill; his son became army horse commissioner.

sentences.zh: 甲申，乃集諸將責李湛、伊婁說、張丕以不憂軍事，斥之外縣。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen he gathered the generals and rebuked Li Zhan, Yi Loushuo, and Zhang Pi for not caring for military affairs, sending them out to outer counties.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen he rebuked Li Zhan, Yi Loushuo, and Zhang Pi for neglecting the army and banished them to outer counties.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使第五守進至汴州，宣慰始畢，軍士十餘人呼曰：「兵馬使勤勞無賞，劉沐何人，為行軍司馬！」

translations.literal: The emperor sent palace envoy Diwu Shoujin to Bianzhou; when the comforting address had just ended, more than ten soldiers cried: "The army horse commissioner toiled without reward—who is Liu Mu to be campaigning army marshal!"
translations.idiomatic: Palace envoy Diwu Shoujin reached Bianzhou; as the address ended, soldiers shouted, "The horse commissioner earned no reward—who is Liu Mu to be marshal!"

sentences.zh: 沐懼，陽中風，舁出。

translations.literal: Mu was afraid and pretended to have a stroke; he was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Mu feigned a stroke and was carried out.

sentences.zh: 軍士又呼曰：「倉官劉叔何給納有奸。」

translations.literal: The soldiers cried again: "Granary officer Liu Shuhe's issues were fraudulent in distribution."
translations.idiomatic: They shouted, "Granary officer Liu Shuhe cheated on rations."

sentences.zh: 殺而食之。

translations.literal: They killed and ate him.
translations.idiomatic: They killed and ate him.

sentences.zh: 又欲斫守進，乃止之。

translations.literal: They also wished to hack Shoujin; they were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They nearly killed Shoujin but were stopped.

sentences.zh: 乃又殺伊婁說、張丕。

translations.literal: They then also killed Yi Loushuo and Zhang Pi.
translations.idiomatic: They then killed Yi Loushuo and Zhang Pi.

sentences.zh: 都虞候匡城鄧惟恭與萬榮鄉里相善，萬榮常委謀以腹心，乃亦倚之。

translations.literal: Chief controller Deng Weigong of Kuangcheng was on good terms with Wanrong's home district; Wanrong had long entrusted him with plans as his confidant, and also relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief controller Deng Weigong of Kuangcheng, Wanrong's townsman and confidant, was also relied upon.

sentences.zh: 至是，惟恭與監軍俱文珍，執乃，送京師。

translations.literal: At this time Weigong and Army Supervisor Ju Wenzhen seized Li Nai and sent him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong and army supervisor Ju Wenzhen seized Li Nai and sent him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙未，以東都留守董晉同平章事，兼宣武節度使，以萬榮為太子少保，貶乃虔州司馬。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day yiwei, eastern capital guardian Dong Jin was made fellow grand councillor and concurrent Xuanwu military commissioner; Wanrong was made junior tutor to the heir apparent and Nai was demoted to militia officer of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei in the seventh month, Dong Jin was made fellow councillor and Xuanwu commissioner; Wanrong became junior tutor to the heir apparent and Nai was demoted.

sentences.zh: 丙申，萬榮薨。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Wanrong died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Wanrong died.

sentences.zh: 鄧惟恭既執李乃，遂權軍事，自謂當代萬榮，不遣人迎董晉。

translations.literal: After Weigong had seized Li Nai he took military power himself, believing he would succeed Wanrong, and sent no one to welcome Dong Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong held power and expected to succeed Wanrong; he did not send anyone to welcome Dong Jin.

sentences.zh: 晉既受詔，即也傔從十餘人赴鎮，不用兵衛。

translations.literal: Jin had received the edict and at once set out with a little more than ten attendants to take the command, using no military escort.
translations.idiomatic: Jin set out at once with only a dozen attendants and no escort.

sentences.zh: 至鄭州，迎者不至，鄭州人為晉懼，或勸晉且留觀變。

translations.literal: When he reached Zhengzhou no one came to meet him; the people of Zhengzhou feared for Jin, and some advised him to stay and watch developments.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhengzhou no one met him; locals feared for his safety and urged him to wait.

sentences.zh: 有自汴州出者，言於晉曰：「不可入。」

translations.literal: Someone coming out of Bianzhou said to Jin: "You must not enter."
translations.idiomatic: A man from Bianzhou warned, "Do not enter."

sentences.zh: 晉不對，遂行。

translations.literal: Jin made no reply and went on.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said nothing and went on.

sentences.zh: 惟恭以晉來之速，不及謀。

translations.literal: Weigong, because Jin came so quickly, had no time to plot.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong, taken by surprise at Jin's speed, had no time to plot.

sentences.zh: 晉去城十餘里，惟恭乃帥諸將出迎。

translations.literal: When Jin was a little more than ten li from the city, Weigong then led the generals out to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was ten li from the city, Weigong led the generals out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 晉命惟恭勿下馬，氣色甚和，惟恭差自安。

translations.literal: Jin ordered Weigong not to dismount; his manner was very mild, and Weigong felt somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Jin told Weigong to remain mounted; his manner was mild, and Weigong felt somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 既入，仍委惟恭以軍政。

translations.literal: Once inside he still entrusted military affairs to Weigong.
translations.idiomatic: Once inside he still left military affairs to Weigong.

sentences.zh: 初，劉玄佐增汴州兵至十萬，遇之厚，李萬榮、鄧惟恭每回厚焉。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Xuanzuo had increased Bianzhou troops to one hundred thousand and treated them generously; Li Wanrong and Deng Weigong each in turn did the same.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuanzuo had raised Bianzhou's army to one hundred thousand and treated the men well; Wanrong and Weigong had done the same.

sentences.zh: 士卒驕，不能御，乃置腹心之士，幕於公庭廡下，挾弓執劍以備之，時勞賜酒肉。

translations.literal: The soldiers were arrogant and could not be controlled, so trusted men were posted under the eaves of the public hall with bows and swords at the ready, and were regularly rewarded with wine and meat.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were unruly; trusted men camped under the hall eaves with bows and swords, rewarded with wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 晉至之明日，悉罷之。

translations.literal: The day after Jin arrived he abolished them all.
translations.idiomatic: The day after Jin arrived he dismissed them all.

sentences.zh: 戊威，韓王迥薨。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Prince Han of Han died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Prince Han of Han died.

sentences.zh: 壬子，詔以宣武將士鄧惟恭等有執送李乃功，各遷官賜錢。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, an edict ordered that Xuanwu officers and soldiers including Deng Weigong, for the merit of seizing and sending Li Nai, each be promoted and given money.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, an edict rewarded Xuanwu troops including Weigong for capturing Li Nai with promotions and cash.

sentences.zh: 其為乃所脅，邀逼制使者，皆勿問。

translations.literal: Those who had been coerced by Nai or who had obstructed the edict-bearing envoy were all not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Those coerced by Nai or who had hindered the envoy were not punished.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙未朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the first day yimao of the month, there was an eclipse of the sun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the first day (yimao), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 己巳，以田季安為魏博節度使。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Tian Ji'an was made military commissioner of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Tian Ji'an was made military commissioner of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以汝州刺史陸長源為宣武行軍司馬。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Ruzhou Prefect Lu Changyuan was made Xuanwu campaigning army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Lu Changyuan, prefect of Ruzhou, was made Xuanwu campaigning army marshal.

sentences.zh: 朝議以董晉柔仁多可，恐不能集事，故以長源佐之。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that Dong Jin was gentle, yielding, and agreeable and might not be able to gather affairs; therefore Changyuan was made his assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The court thought Dong Jin too mild to manage the command and sent Changyuan to assist him.

sentences.zh: 長源性剛刻，多更張舊事。

translations.literal: Changyuan was by nature harsh and severe and changed many old practices.
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan was harsh and overturned many old customs.

sentences.zh: 晉初皆許之，案成則命且罷，由是軍中得安。

translations.literal: Jin at first agreed to everything; when the plan was drawn up he would order it suspended, and thus the army was kept at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Jin agreed at first, then suspended each plan once drafted—keeping the army calm.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，門下侍郎、同平章事趙憬薨。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow Grand Councillor Zhao Jing died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Zhao Jing, vice director of the Secretariat and fellow grand councillor, died.

sentences.zh: 初，上不欲生代節度使，常自擇行軍司馬以為儲帥。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor did not wish military commissioners to succeed their fathers and commonly chose campaigning army marshals himself as stored commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not let commands pass father to son and usually picked the campaigning marshal as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 李景略為河東行軍司馬，李說忌之。

translations.literal: Li Jinglue was Hedong campaigning army marshal; Li Shuo was jealous of him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglue was Hedong's campaigning marshal; Li Shuo resented him.

sentences.zh: 回鶻梅錄入貢，過太原，說與之宴，梅錄爭坐次，說不能遏。

translations.literal: A Uyghur Meilu came to present tribute and passed through Taiyuan. Shuo feasted him; Meilu disputed seating order and Shuo could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: A Uyghur Meilu came to court via Taiyuan. At Shuo's banquet Meilu quarreled over precedence and Shuo could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 景略叱之，梅錄識其聲，趨前拜之曰：「非豐州李端公邪！」

translations.literal: Jinglue rebuked him. Meilu recognized his voice, hurried forward, and bowed, saying: "Are you not Vice Director Li of Fengzhou!"
translations.idiomatic: Jinglue rebuked him. Meilu recognized his voice, bowed, and said, "Are you not Director Li of Fengzhou!"

sentences.zh: 又拜，遂就下坐。

translations.literal: He bowed again and then took the lower seat.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed again and took the lower seat.

sentences.zh: 座中皆屬目於景略。

translations.literal: All at the table fixed their eyes on Jinglue.
translations.idiomatic: All eyes turned to Jinglue.

sentences.zh: 說益不平，乃厚賂中尉竇文場，使去之。

translations.literal: Shuo was all the more displeased and therefore bribed Chief Protector Dou Wenchang heavily to have him removed.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo, bitter, bribed Dou Wenchang to remove him.

sentences.zh: 會有傳回鶻將入寇者，上憂之，以豐州當虜沖，擇可守者。

translations.literal: It happened that there was talk that the Uyghurs would invade; the emperor was worried. Fengzhou faced the barbarian thrust and he sought someone who could defend it.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that the Uyghurs would invade; Fengzhou lay on the frontier and the emperor sought a defender.

sentences.zh: 文場因薦景略。

translations.literal: Wenchang thereupon recommended Jinglue.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang recommended Jinglue.

sentences.zh: 九月，甲午，以景略為豐州都防禦使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jiawu, Jinglue was made defense commissioner of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiawu, Jinglue was made defense commissioner of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 窮邊氣寒，土瘠民貧，景略以勤儉帥眾，二歲之後，儲備完實，雄於北邊。

translations.literal: The remote border was cold in climate, the soil poor and the people impoverished. Jinglue led the masses with diligence and thrift; within two years stores were full and he was strongest on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier was cold and poor; Jinglue led by thrift, and within two years his stores were full and he dominated the north.

sentences.zh: 盧邁得風疾，庚子，賈耽私忌，宰相絕班，上遣中使召主書承旨。

translations.literal: Lu Mai had a wind ailment. On the day gengzi, because of Jia Dan's private taboo the chancellors broke formation; the emperor sent a palace envoy to summon the chief clerk and drafting officer.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Mai was ill. On gengzi, Jia Dan's taboo broke the chancellors' formation; the emperor summoned the drafting clerk.

sentences.zh: 丙午，戶部書尚、判度支裴延齡卒，中外相賀，上獨悼惜之。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Minister of Revenue and Commissioner of Public Revenue Pei Yanling died. Inside and outside the court congratulated one another; the emperor alone mourned and regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Pei Yanling died. Court and country rejoiced; only the emperor grieved.

sentences.zh: 壬子，吐蕃寇慶州。

translations.literal: On the day renzi, the Tibetans raided Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Tibetans raided Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲戌，以諫議大夫崔損、給事中趙宗儒並同平章事。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiaxu, Remonstrance Officer Cui Sun and Drafting Attendant Zhao Zongru were both made fellow grand councillors.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiaxu, Cui Sun and Zhao Zongru were made fellow grand councillors.

sentences.zh: 損，玄□之弟孫也，嘗為裴延齡所薦，故用之。

translations.literal: Sun was a great-grandson of Cui Xuanwei and had once been recommended by Pei Yanling; therefore he was used.
translations.idiomatic: Sun was a descendant of Cui Xuanwei and had been Yanling's protégé—hence his appointment.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙未，以右補闕韋渠牟為左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day yimao, Right Supplemener Wei Qumou was made left remonstrance officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yimao, Wei Qumou was made left remonstrance officer.

sentences.zh: 上自陸贄貶官，尤不任宰相，自御史、刺呼、縣令以上皆自選用，中書行文書而已。

translations.literal: Since Lu Zhi's demotion the emperor especially would not rely on chancellors. From censors, prefects, and county magistrates upward he chose them all himself; the Secretariat only drafted documents.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Zhi's fall the emperor stopped trusting chancellors. He picked officials himself from censors down to magistrates; the Secretariat only drafted paperwork.

sentences.zh: 然深居禁中，所取信者裴延齡、李齊運、戶部郎中王紹、司農卿李實、翰林學士韋執誼及渠牟，皆權傾宰相，趨附盈門。

translations.literal: Yet dwelling deep in the forbidden quarters, those he trusted were Pei Yanling, Li Qiyun, Revenue Bureau director Wang Shao, Minister of Agriculture Li Shi, Hanlin Academician Wei Zhiyi, and Qumou—all wielded power equal to chancellors, and those who rushed to attach to them filled their gates.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted Yanling, Qiyun, Wang Shao, Li Shi, Wei Zhiyi, and Qumou—each as powerful as a chancellor, with crowds at their gates.

sentences.zh: 紹謹密無損益，實狡險掊克；

translations.literal: Shao was cautious and secretive without benefit or harm; Shi was crafty, dangerous, and extortionate;
translations.idiomatic: Shao was cautious but useless; Shi was cunning and grasping;

sentences.zh: 執誼以文章與上唱和，年二十餘，自右拾遺召入翰林；

translations.literal: Zhiyi harmonized with the emperor through literature; in his twenties he was summoned from right remembrancer into the Hanlin;
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi pleased the emperor with verse; in his twenties he entered the Hanlin;

sentences.zh: 渠牟形神恌躁，尤為上所親狎，上每對執政，漏不過三刻，渠牟奏事率至六刻，語笑款狎往往聞外，所薦引鹹不次遷擢，率皆庸鄙之士。

translations.literal: Qumou was reckless in form and spirit and especially intimate with the emperor. Whenever the emperor met the chief ministers the leak did not exceed three quarters of an hour; Qumou's reports usually lasted six quarters, and familiar laughter was often heard outside. Those he recommended were all promoted out of turn, mostly vulgar and base men.
translations.idiomatic: Qumou was flighty and the emperor's favorite; his audiences ran twice as long as the chancellors', and his nominees were vulgar men rushed into office.

sentences.zh: 宣武都虞侯鄧惟恭內不自安，潛結將士二百餘人謀作亂。

translations.literal: Xuanwu chief controller Deng Weigong was uneasy within himself and secretly joined more than two hundred officers and soldiers to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Weigong plotted rebellion with two hundred officers.

sentences.zh: 事覺，董晉悉捕斬其黨，械惟恭送京師。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered, Dong Jin arrested and executed the whole faction and sent Weigong to the capital in cangues.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jin executed the plotters and sent Weigong to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔免死，汀州安置。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, an edict spared his life and exiled him to Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, he was spared and exiled to Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十貞元十三年（

translations.literal: Divine Martial and Sagacious Literary Emperor Dezong 10, thirteenth year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, thirteenth year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 丁丑，公元七九七年）

translations.literal: dingchou, corresponding to AD 797)
translations.idiomatic: dingchou, AD 797)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬寅，吐蕃遣使請和親，上以吐蕃數負約，不許。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day renyin, Tibet sent envoys requesting marriage alliance; because the Tibetans had repeatedly broken treaties, the emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on renyin, Tibet asked for a marriage alliance; the emperor refused, citing broken treaties.

sentences.zh: 上以方渠、合道、木波皆吐蕃要路，欲城之，使問邠寧節度使楊朝晟：「須幾何兵？」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to fortify Fangqu, Hedao, and Mubo—all key Tibetan routes—and asked Binning Military Commissioner Yang Chaocheng: "How many troops are needed?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to build forts at Fangqu, Hedao, and Mubo and asked Yang Chaocheng how many troops he needed."

sentences.zh: 對曰：「邠寧兵足以城之，不煩他道。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Binning's troops are enough to build them; other circuits need not be troubled."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Binning's troops suffice; no other circuit is needed."

sentences.zh: 上復使問之曰：「曏城鹽州，用兵七萬，僅能集事。

translations.literal: The emperor again asked: "Formerly in fortifying Yanzhou seven thousand troops were used and barely succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Building Yanzhou took seventy thousand men—why so few now?

sentences.zh: 今三城尤逼虜境，兵當倍之，事更相反，何也？」

translations.literal: Now these three cities press even closer on barbarian territory—the troops ought to be doubled, and the matter is the opposite—why?"
translations.idiomatic: These forts face the frontier—shouldn't you need twice as many?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「城鹽州之眾，虜皆知之。

translations.literal: He replied: "The masses who built Yanzhou were all known to the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The Yanzhou army was known to the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 今發本鎮兵，不旬日至塞下，出其不意而城之。

translations.literal: Now if I send this circuit's troops, within ten days they will reach the border, build the cities by surprise.
translations.idiomatic: Send only Binning's men—they can reach the border in ten days and build before the enemy knows.

sentences.zh: 虜謂吾眾亦不減七萬，其眾未集，不敢輕來犯我。

translations.literal: The barbarians will think our numbers are no fewer than seventy thousand; before their masses gather they will not dare lightly come to attack us.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet will assume we still have seventy thousand men and dare not attack until they mass.

sentences.zh: 不過三旬，吾城已畢，留兵戍之，虜雖至，無能為也。

translations.literal: In no more than thirty days our forts will be finished; we leave troops to garrison them, and even if the barbarians come they can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In thirty days the forts will stand; garrisons can hold off any attack.

sentences.zh: 城旁草盡，不能久留，虜退則運芻糧以實之，此萬全之策也。

translations.literal: Grass beside the forts will be exhausted; they cannot stay long. When the barbarians withdraw we haul fodder and grain to fill the stores—this is the plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: Grass will be gone—they cannot linger. When they leave we stock the forts. That is the sure plan.

sentences.zh: 若大集諸道兵，逾月始至，虜亦集眾而來，與我爭戰。
