translations.literal: If we mass troops from many circuits and they arrive only after a month, the barbarians too will gather and come to fight us.
translations.idiomatic: Mass troops from many circuits and Tibet will meet us in battle.

sentences.zh: 勝負未可知，何暇築城哉！」

translations.literal: Victory and defeat cannot be known—how then could we build forts!"
translations.idiomatic: Who could build forts then!"

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 二月，朝晟分軍為三，各築一城。

translations.literal: In the second month Chaocheng divided the army in three, each building one city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Chaocheng split his force to build three forts.

sentences.zh: 軍吏曰：「方渠無井，不可屯軍。」

translations.literal: Army clerks said: "Fangqu has no wells and troops cannot be stationed."
translations.idiomatic: Officers said, "Fangqu has no wells—troops cannot camp there."

sentences.zh: 判官孟子周曰：「方渠承平之時，居人成市，無井何以聚人乎！」

translations.literal: Judge Meng Zizhou said: "In peaceful times Fangqu had residents forming a market—without wells how could people gather!"
translations.idiomatic: Judge Meng Zizhou said, "In peace it was a market town—how did people live without wells!"

sentences.zh: 命浚眢井，果得甘泉。

translations.literal: He ordered old wells dug and indeed obtained sweet springs.
translations.idiomatic: They dug old wells and found sweet water.

sentences.zh: 三月，三城成。

translations.literal: In the third month the three cities were completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the three forts were finished.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，庚申，楊朝晟軍還至馬嶺，吐蕃始出兵追之，相拒數月而去。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day gengshen, when Chaocheng's army returned to Maling the Tibetans first sent troops in pursuit; they faced off for several months and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on gengshen, Tibet pursued Chaocheng to Maling; they faced off for months.

sentences.zh: 朝晟遂城馬嶺而還，開地三百里，皆如其素。

translations.literal: Chaocheng then fortified Maling and returned, opening three hundred li of land—all as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Chaocheng fortified Maling and opened three hundred li of territory, as he had promised.

sentences.zh: 庚午，義成節度使李復薨。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Yicheng Military Commissioner Li Fu died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Li Fu, military commissioner of Yicheng, died.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，以陝虢觀察使姚南仲為義成節度使。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Shaan-Guo Observation Commissioner Yao Nanzhong was made Yicheng military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Yao Nanzhong was made military commissioner of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 監軍薛盈珍方大會，聞之，言曰：「姚大夫書生，豈將才也！」

translations.literal: Army Supervisor Xue Yingzhen was holding a great assembly when he heard of it and said: "Grandee Yao is a bookish man—how can he be a general!"
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Xue Yingzhen sneered, "Yao is a scholar—not general material!"

sentences.zh: 判官盧坦私謂人曰：「姚大夫外雖柔，中甚剛，監之侵之，必不受。

translations.literal: Judge Lu Tan said privately to others: "Grandee Yao is soft outside but very hard within; if the supervisor insults him he will not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Lu Tan warned, "Yao is soft outside but hard within—provoke him and trouble follows.

sentences.zh: 軍府之禍，自此始矣，吾恐為所留。」

translations.literal: The military headquarters' disaster begins from this; I fear I will be detained."
translations.idiomatic: Disaster starts here; I may be held."

sentences.zh: 遂自他道潛去。

translations.literal: He then left secretly by another road.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped away by another route.

sentences.zh: 南仲果以牒請之，不遇，得免。

translations.literal: Nanzhong indeed sent a dispatch requesting him; he was not found and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong summoned him; he was gone.

sentences.zh: 既而盈珍與南仲有隙，幕府多以罪貶，有死者。

translations.literal: Later Yingzhen and Nanzhong had a rift; many in the staff were demoted for crimes, and some died.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen and Nanzhong clashed; staff were punished and some died.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃贊普乞立贊卒，子足之煎立。

translations.literal: The Tibetan king Tridé Tsuktsen died; his son Footsie was installed.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetan king Tridé Tsuktsen died; his son Footsie succeeded.

sentences.zh: 六月，壬午，韋皋奏吐蕃入寇，巂州刺史曹高仕破之於台登城下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day renwu, Wei Gao reported Tibet invading; Cizhou Prefect Cao Gaoshi defeated them below Taideng City.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Wei Gao reported a Tibetan raid; Cao Gaoshi defeated them at Taideng.

sentences.zh: 光祿少卿同正張茂宗，茂昭之弟也，許尚義章公主；

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Tongzheng Zhang Maozong was Maozhao's younger brother and was betrothed to Princess Yizhang;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Maozong, Maozhao's brother, was betrothed to Princess Yizhang;

sentences.zh: 未成婚，茂宗母卒，遺表請終嘉禮，上許之。

translations.literal: before the marriage Maozong's mother died. Her final memorial requested completion of the auspicious rites; the emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: before the wedding his mother died; her dying request to complete the rites was granted.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，癸酉，起復茂宗左衛將軍同正。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the day guiyou, Maozong was recalled from mourning as acting left Guards general.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on guiyou, Maozong was recalled to office as acting left Guards general.

sentences.zh: 左拾遣義興蔣乂上疏諫，以為：「兵革之急，古有墨衰從事者，未聞附馬起復尚主也。」

translations.literal: Left Remembrancer Jiang Yi of Yixing submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying: "In the urgency of war, antiquity had those who wore ink mourning while serving—but never have I heard of an imperial son-in-law recalled from mourning to marry a princess."
translations.idiomatic: Remembrancer Jiang Yi objected: "Soldiers may wear ink mourning in war, but no imperial son-in-law should leave mourning to marry."

sentences.zh: 上遣中使諭之，不止，乃特召對於延英，謂曰：「人間多借吉成婚者，卿何執此之堅？」

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to instruct him; he did not stop. He was specially summoned to audience in Yanying and told: "Among the people many borrow auspicious days to marry—why are you so stubborn on this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's envoy failed; summoned to Yanying, the emperor said, "Commoners often marry on lucky days—why are you so rigid?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「婚姻、喪紀，人之大倫，吉凶不可瀆也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Marriage and mourning observance are the great human relations; auspicious and inauspicious must not be profaned.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang replied, "Marriage and mourning are great rites—auspicious and inauspicious must not be mixed."

sentences.zh: 委巷之家，不知禮教，其女孤貧無恃，或有借吉從人，未聞男子借吉娶婦者也。」

translations.literal: In alley households who do not know ritual teaching, if a girl is orphaned and poor with no support, some borrow auspicious days to follow a man—but never have I heard of a man borrowing auspicious days to take a wife."
translations.idiomatic: Poor girls may marry on borrowed lucky days—but never a man leaving mourning to wed.

sentences.zh: 太常博士韋彤、裴堪復上疏諫。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices academics Wei Tong and Pei Kan again submitted memorials remonstrating.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Tong and Pei Kan of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices protested again.

sentences.zh: 上不悅，命趣下嫁之期，辛巳，成婚。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and ordered the wedding date hastened. On the day xinsi the marriage was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hastened the wedding; on xinsi they married.

sentences.zh: 九月，己丑，中書侍郎、同平章事盧邁以疾罷為太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day jichou, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow Grand Councillor Lu Mai was removed for illness and made guest of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Lu Mai was dismissed for illness and made tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，淮西節度使吳少誠擅開刀溝入汝，上遣中使諭止之，不從。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Huai-Hsi Military Commissioner Wu Shaoqing on his own authority opened the Daogou channel into Ru; the emperor sent a palace envoy to instruct and stop him, but he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, Wu Shaoqing of Huai-Hsi opened the Daogou canal into Ru without permission and ignored the emperor's envoy.

sentences.zh: 命兵部郎中盧群往詰之，少誠曰：「開此水，大利於人。」

translations.literal: He ordered Ministry of War director Lu Qun to go and question him. Shaoqing said: "Opening this water greatly benefits the people."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qun was sent to rebuke him. Shaoqing said, "This canal greatly benefits the people."

sentences.zh: 群曰：「君令臣行，雖利，人臣敢專乎！

translations.literal: Qun said: "The ruler orders and the minister acts—even if it benefits, how dare a minister act on his own!
translations.idiomatic: Qun said, "The ruler commands—even if it helps, how dare a subject act alone!

sentences.zh: 公承天子之令而不從，何以使下吏從公之令乎！」

translations.literal: You receive the Son of Heaven's order and do not obey—how can you make subordinate officers obey your orders!"
translations.idiomatic: You disobey the Son of Heaven—how can you demand obedience from your men!"

sentences.zh: 少誠遽為之罷役。

translations.literal: Shaoqing hastily stopped the work for him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing stopped the work at once.

sentences.zh: 十二月，徐州節度使張建封入朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Xuzhou Military Commissioner Zhang Jianfeng entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou came to court.

sentences.zh: 先是，宮中市外間物，令官吏主之，隨給其直。

translations.literal: Earlier, within the palace market goods from outside were bought and officials were put in charge, paying the fair price as goods were supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Once the palace bought outside goods through officials at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 比歲以宦者為使，謂之宮市，抑買人物，稍不如本估。

translations.literal: In recent years eunuchs were used as agents, called "palace market," buying goods at prices somewhat below true value.
translations.idiomatic: Later eunuchs called "palace market" bought below fair value.

sentences.zh: 其後不復行文書，置白望數百人於兩市及要鬧坊曲，閱人所賣物，但稱宮市，則斂手付與，真偽不復可辯，無敢問所從來及論價之高下者，率用直百錢物買人直數千物，多以紅紫染故衣、敗繒，尺寸裂而給之，仍索進奉門戶及腳價錢。

translations.literal: Later they no longer used documents at all but placed several hundred "white watchers" in the two markets and busy wards and lanes, inspecting what people sold; they need only say "palace market" and people would fold their hands and yield the goods. True and false could no longer be distinguished; none dared ask whence they came or dispute the price. They commonly used goods worth a hundred cash to buy goods worth thousands from people, often giving purple and red dyed old clothes and torn silks cut to size, and still demanded "tribute gate" fees and porterage money.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of "white watchers" seized goods as "palace market" without documents or fair price—paying pennies for dollars in dyed rags and demanding gate fees.

sentences.zh: 人將物詣市，至有空手而歸者，名為宮市，其實奪之。

translations.literal: When people brought goods to market some returned empty-handed; though called palace market, in fact it was robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants often went home empty-handed—palace market was robbery.

sentences.zh: 商賈有良貨，皆深匿之。

translations.literal: Merchants with good goods all hid them deep away.
translations.idiomatic: Good goods were hidden away.

sentences.zh: 每敕使出，雖沽漿、賣餅者皆撤業閉門。

translations.literal: Whenever edict envoys went out, even sellers of gruel and cakes shut their trade and closed their doors.
translations.idiomatic: When palace agents appeared, even food sellers closed shop.

sentences.zh: 嘗有農夫以驢負柴，宦者稱宮市取之，與絹數尺，又就索門戶，仍邀驢送柴至內。

translations.literal: Once a farmer carried firewood on a donkey; a eunuch called it palace market and took it, giving several feet of silk, then also demanded gate fees and still pressed the donkey to carry the firewood into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: A farmer's donkey load of firewood was seized for a few feet of silk, then they took the donkey to haul wood inside.

sentences.zh: 農夫啼泣，以所得絹與之，不肯受，曰：「須得爾驢。」

translations.literal: The farmer wept and gave him the silk he had received; he would not accept it and said: "I must have your donkey."
translations.idiomatic: The farmer wept and offered back the silk; they refused: "We want the donkey."

sentences.zh: 農夫曰：「我有父母妻子，待此然後食。

translations.literal: The farmer said: "I have parents, wife, and children—we wait on this to eat.
translations.idiomatic: The farmer said, "My family waits on this to eat.

sentences.zh: 今以柴與汝，不取直而歸，汝尚不肯，我有死而已。」

translations.literal: Now I give you the firewood without taking payment and you still will not agree—you will not have me until I am dead."
translations.idiomatic: I give you the wood and you still refuse—only my death remains."

sentences.zh: 遂毆宦者。

translations.literal: He then beat the eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the eunuch.

sentences.zh: 街吏擒以聞，詔黜宦者，賜農夫絹十匹。

translations.literal: Street officers seized him and reported; an edict demoted the eunuch and gave the farmer ten bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Street officers seized him and reported; the eunuch was demoted and the farmer given ten bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 然宮市亦不為之改，諫官御史數奏疏諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Yet the palace market was not changed for this. Remonstrating officials and investigating censors repeatedly submitted memorials remonstrating; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the palace market continued unchanged; censors protested repeatedly, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 建封入朝，具奏之，上頗嘉納，以問戶部侍郎判度支蘇弁，弁希宦者意，對曰：「京師游手萬家，無土著生業，仰宮市取給。」

translations.literal: Jianfeng entered court and reported it fully in a memorial; the emperor was quite pleased to accept it and asked Vice Minister of Revenue and Commissioner of Public Revenue Su Bian. Bian, hoping to please the eunuchs, replied: "In the capital there are tens of thousands of idlers without fixed native occupations who rely on the palace market for their livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng reported the abuses; the emperor asked Su Bian, who curried favor with eunuchs and said tens of thousands of idlers depended on the palace market."

sentences.zh: 上信之，故凡言宮市者皆不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor believed this; therefore all who spoke of the palace market were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him and ignored all further complaints about the palace market.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十貞元十四年（

translations.literal: Divine Martial and Sagacious Literary Emperor Dezong 10, fourteenth year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, fourteenth year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 戊寅，公元七九八年）

translations.literal: wuyin, corresponding to AD 798)
translations.idiomatic: wuyin, AD 798)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，乙亥，名申、光、蔡軍曰彰義。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on the day yihai, the Shen, Guang, and Cai armies were named Zhangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the second month, on yihai, the Shen, Guang, and Cai armies were renamed Zhangyi.

sentences.zh: 夏，閏五月，庚申，以神策行營節度使韓全義為夏、綏、銀、宥節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the intercalary fifth month, on the day gengshen, Shence campaigning army commissioner Han Quanyi was made military commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month, on gengshen, Han Quanyi was made commissioner of Xia, Sui, Yin, and You.

sentences.zh: 全義時屯長武城，詔帥其眾赴鎮。

translations.literal: Quanyi was then encamped at Changwu Fort; an edict ordered him to lead his masses to take up the command.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi was at Changwu Fort; he was ordered to take up his command.

sentences.zh: 士卒以夏州磧鹵，又盛夏，不樂徙居。

translations.literal: The soldiers considered Xiazhou's desert brine harsh and that it was also midsummer; they were unwilling to move and settle.
translations.idiomatic: The troops hated Xiazhou's salty desert and the summer heat and refused to move.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，軍亂，殺大將王棲巖等，全義逾城走。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou the army mutinied and killed the great generals Wang Qiyan and others; Quanyi leaped over the wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the army mutinied, killed Wang Qiyan and others, and Quanyi fled over the wall.

sentences.zh: 都虞侯高崇文誅首亂者，眾然後定。

translations.literal: Chief controller Gao Chongwen executed the ringleaders; the masses were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen executed the ringleaders and restored order.

sentences.zh: 崇文，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Chongwen was a man of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chongwen was from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以崇文為長武城都知兵馬使，不降敕，令中使口宣授之。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Chongwen was made Changwu Fort's commander of all army horse affairs, without a descending edict—the order was orally proclaimed by a palace envoy.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Chongwen was made Changwu commander by oral edict, without written appointment.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬申，給事中、同平章事趙宗儒罷為右庶子，以工部侍郎鄭餘慶為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day renshen, Drafting Attendant and Fellow Grand Councillor Zhao Zongru was removed and made right heir apparent tutor; Minister of Works Vice Director Zheng Yuqing was made vice director of the Secretariat and fellow grand councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen in the seventh month, Zhao Zongru was demoted and Zheng Yuqing made fellow grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 八月，初置左、右神策統軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the left and right Shence army commanders were first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the left and right Shence army commanders were first established.

sentences.zh: 時禁軍戍邊者，稟賜優厚，諸將多請遙隸神策軍，稱行營，皆統於中尉，其軍遂至十五萬人。

translations.literal: At that time forbidden-army troops on frontier garrison received generous rations and gifts; many generals asked to be remotely attached to the Shence Army and called it campaigning armies—all under the chief protectors—until the army reached one hundred fifty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops sought Shence affiliation for better pay; the Shence army grew to one hundred fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹吳湊屢言宮市之弊，請委之府縣。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Governor Wu Cou repeatedly spoke of the palace market's abuses and asked that it be entrusted to the prefecture and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Metropolitan governor Wu Cou repeatedly denounced the palace market and asked that civil officials handle it.

sentences.zh: 宦者言湊屢奏宮市，皆右金吾都知趙洽、田秀巖之謀也。

translations.literal: The eunuchs said Cou's repeated memorials on the palace market were all plots of Jinwu chief controllers Zhao Qia and Tian Xiuyan.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs claimed Cou was acting for Zhao Qia and Tian Xiuyan of the Jinwu guard.

sentences.zh: 丙午，洽、秀巖坐流天德軍。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Qia and Xiuyan were exiled to Tiande Army for their crime.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Qia and Xiuyan were exiled to Tiande Army.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙申，以陝虢觀察使-{于}-頔為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day bingshen, Shaan-Guo Observation Commissioner Yu Di was made Shannan East Circuit military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen in the ninth month, Yu Di was made military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，札王倕薨。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, Prince Zha of Zha died.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Prince Zha died.

sentences.zh: 彰義節度使吳少誠遣兵掠壽州霍山，殺鎮遏使謝詳，侵地二十餘里，置兵鎮守。

translations.literal: Zhangyi Military Commissioner Wu Shaoqing sent troops to plunder Huoshan in Shouzhou, killed pacification commissioner Xie Xiang, encroached on territory more than twenty li, and placed troops to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shaoqing raided Shouzhou, killed Xie Xiang, and seized territory.

sentences.zh: 太學生薛約師事司業陽城，坐言事，徙連州，城送之郊外。

translations.literal: Imperial University student Xue Yue studied under Directorate of Education Vice Director Yang Cheng and was punished for speaking on affairs, being banished to Lianzhou; Cheng saw him off beyond the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: Student Xue Yue, Yang Cheng's pupil, was banished to Lianzhou; Cheng escorted him beyond the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 上以城黨罪人，己巳，左遷城道州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Cheng had befriended a criminal, on the day jisi demoted Cheng to prefect of Daozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi the emperor demoted Cheng to prefect of Daozhou for befriending a punished man.

sentences.zh: 城治民如治家，州之賦稅不登，觀察使數加誚讓，城自署其考曰：「撫字心勞，征科政拙，考下下。」

translations.literal: Cheng governed the people as he would a household. The prefecture's taxes were not collected; the observation commissioner repeatedly rebuked him. Cheng himself wrote his evaluation: "Comforting the people exhausted my heart; collecting levies my policy was clumsy—evaluation: lowest lowest."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng governed like a family head. When taxes fell short the observer rebuked him; Cheng rated himself lowest for gentle rule but poor collection."

sentences.zh: 觀察使遣判官督其賦，至州，城先自囚於獄。

translations.literal: The observation commissioner sent a judge to press for taxes. When he reached the prefecture, Cheng had already imprisoned himself.
translations.idiomatic: The observer sent a tax collector; Cheng had already jailed himself.

sentences.zh: 判官大驚，馳入，謁城於獄曰：「使君何罪！

translations.literal: The judge was greatly alarmed, galloped in, and visited Cheng in prison, saying: "What crime has the lord committed!
translations.idiomatic: “The judge rushed to the jail asking what crime Cheng had committed.

sentences.zh: 某奉命來侯安否耳。」

translations.literal: I was ordered to come only to inquire after your health."
translations.idiomatic: I was only sent to inquire after your health."

sentences.zh: 留一二日未去，城不復歸。

translations.literal: He stayed one or two days without leaving; Cheng did not return to his quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed days; Cheng would not leave the jail.

sentences.zh: 館門外有故門扇橫地，城晝夜坐臥其上，判官不自安，辭去。

translations.literal: Outside the hostel gate was an old door panel lying on the ground; day and night Cheng sat and lay on it. The judge was ill at ease and took his leave.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sat on a door panel outside the jail until the judge fled.

sentences.zh: 其後又遣它判官往按之，它判官載妻子行中道逸去。

translations.literal: Later another judge was sent to investigate; that judge loaded his wife and children and fled on the road midway.
translations.idiomatic: A later investigator fled midway with his family.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁酉，通王諶薨。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day dingyou, Prince Tong of Tong died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on dingyou, Prince Tong died.

sentences.zh: 庚子，夏州節度使韓全義奏破吐蕃於鹽州西北。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Xiazhou Military Commissioner Han Quanyi reported defeating Tibet northwest of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Han Quanyi reported defeating Tibet northwest of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 明州鎮將栗金皇殺刺史盧雲，誘山越作亂，攻陷浙東州縣。

translations.literal: Mingzhou garrison commander Li Jinhuang killed Prefect Lu Yun, incited mountain Yue to rebel, and attacked and seized Zhedong prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinhuang killed the Mingzhou prefect and led Yue tribes in revolt across Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十貞元十五年（

translations.literal: Divine Martial and Sagacious Literary Emperor Dezong 10, fifteenth year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, fifteenth year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 己卯，公元七九九年）

translations.literal: jimao, corresponding to AD 799)
translations.idiomatic: jimao, AD 799)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲寅，雅王逸薨。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day jiayin, Prince Ya of Ya died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on jiayin, Prince Ya died.

sentences.zh: 二月，丁丑，宣武節度使董晉薨。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day dingchou, Xuanwu Military Commissioner Dong Jin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on dingchou, Dong Jin of Xuanwu died.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，以其行軍司馬陸長源為節度使。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, his campaigning army marshal Lu Changyuan was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Lu Changyuan was made military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 長源性刻急。

translations.literal: Changyuan was by nature harsh and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Changyuan was harsh and severe.

sentences.zh: 恃才傲物。

translations.literal: He relied on talent and was arrogant toward others.
translations.idiomatic: He was talented and arrogant.

sentences.zh: 判官孟叔度，輕佻淫縱，好慢侮將士，軍中皆惡之。

translations.literal: Judge Meng Shudu was frivolous, lewd, and unrestrained and liked to insult generals lightly; the army all hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Meng Shudu was dissolute and insulted the officers, who hated him.

sentences.zh: 董晉薨，長源知留後，揚言曰：「將士弛慢日久，當以法齊之耳！」

translations.literal: When Dong Jin died, Changyuan took charge as acting commissioner and declared: "The officers and soldiers have been lax a long time—I shall bring them into line with the law!"
translations.idiomatic: As acting commissioner Changyuan announced he would discipline the long-lax troops by law."

sentences.zh: 眾皆懼。

translations.literal: The masses were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were terrified.

sentences.zh: 或勸之發財以勞軍，長源曰：「我豈效河北賊，以錢買健兒求節鉞邪！」

translations.literal: Some advised him to distribute wealth to reward the army. Changyuan said: "Would I imitate the bandits of Hebei, buying stalwart men with money to seek the commander's baton!"
translations.idiomatic: Advisers urged him to pay the troops; he refused to buy loyalty like Hebei warlords."

sentences.zh: 故事，主帥薨，給軍士布以制服，長源命給其直。

translations.literal: By precedent when a commander-in-chief died, cloth was given the soldiers for mourning garments; Changyuan ordered cash given for the cloth value.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the army received mourning cloth; Changyuan paid cash instead.

sentences.zh: 叔度高鹽直，下布直，人不過得鹽三二斤。

translations.literal: Shudu raised the salt price and lowered the cloth price; a man received no more than two or three jin of salt.
translations.idiomatic: Shudu inflated salt prices and cut cloth payments to a few pounds of salt per man.

sentences.zh: 軍中怨怒，長源亦不為之備。

translations.literal: The army was resentful and angry; Changyuan also made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The army seethed; Changyuan made no preparations.

sentences.zh: 是日，軍士作亂，殺長源、叔度，臠食之，立盡。

translations.literal: That day the soldiers mutinied, killed Changyuan and Shudu, dismembered and ate them, and consumed them entirely.
translations.idiomatic: That day the troops mutinied, killed Changyuan and Shudu, and devoured their bodies.

sentences.zh: 監軍俱文珍以宋州刺史劉逸准久為宣武大將，得眾心，密書召之。

translations.literal: Army Supervisor Ju Wenzhen, because Songzhou Prefect Liu Yizhun had long been a great Xuanwu general and had the army's hearts, secretly wrote to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Wenzhen secretly summoned Liu Yizhun, a popular Songzhou general.

sentences.zh: 逸准引兵徑入汴州，亂眾乃定。

translations.literal: Yizhun led troops straight into Bianzhou; the mutinous masses were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhun entered Bianzhou and restored order.

sentences.zh: 以常州刺史李錡為浙西觀察使、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: Changzhou Prefect Li Qi was made Zhexi observation commissioner and salt and iron transport commissioner for all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi was made Zhexi observer and salt-and-iron transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 錡，國貞之子也。

translations.literal: Qi was the son of Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was Guozhen's son.

sentences.zh: 閒廄、宮苑使李齊運受其賂數十萬，薦之於上，故用之。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the imperial stud and palace parks Li Qiyun received his bribes of several hundred thousand and recommended him to the emperor; therefore he was used.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiyun took hundreds of thousands in bribes and recommended Qi to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 錡刻剝以事進奉，上由是悅之。

translations.literal: Qi extorted and scraped to make presentation offerings; the emperor was therefore pleased with him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi extorted for tribute and won the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，浙東觀察使裴肅擒栗鍠於台州，送京師，斬之。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Zhedong Observation Commissioner Pei Su captured Li Huang at Taizhou, sent him to the capital, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Pei Su captured Li Huang at Taizhou and executed him in the capital.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以劉逸准為宣武節度使，賜名全諒。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Liu Yizhun was made Xuanwu military commissioner and granted the name Quanliang.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Liu Yizhun was made Xuanwu commissioner and named Quanliang.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲寅，吳少誠遣兵襲唐州，殺監軍邵國朝、鎮遏使張嘉瑜，掠百姓千餘人而去。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day jiayin, Wu Shaoqing sent troops to raid Tangzhou, killed army supervisor Shao Guochao and pacification commissioner Zhang Jiayu, and carried off more than a thousand common people.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Shaoqing raided Tangzhou, killed officials, and abducted a thousand people.

sentences.zh: 戊午，昭義節度使王虔休薨。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, Zhaoyi Military Commissioner Wang Qianxiu died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, Wang Qianxiu of Zhaoyi died.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以河陽、懷州節度使李元淳為昭義節度使。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Heyang and Huaizhou Military Commissioner Li Yuanchun was made Zhaoyi military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Li Yuanchun was made military commissioner of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸未，以安州刺史伊慎為安、黃等州節度使。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day guimao, Anzhou Prefect Yi Shen was made military commissioner of An, Huang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao in the fourth month, Yi Shen was made commissioner of An and Huang.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，山南西道節度使嚴震薨。

translations.literal: On the day guisi, Shannan West Circuit Military Commissioner Yan Zhen died.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Yan Zhen of Shannan West Circuit died.

sentences.zh: 南詔異牟尋遣使與韋皋約共擊吐蕃，皋以兵糧未集，請俟它年。

translations.literal: Nanzhao Yimouxun sent envoys to agree with Wei Gao to strike Tibet jointly; Gao, because troops and grain were not gathered, asked to wait until another year.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun proposed joint action with Wei Gao against Tibet; Gao asked to wait for supplies.

sentences.zh: 山南西道都虞候嚴礪諂事嚴震，震病，使知留後，遺表薦之。

translations.literal: Shannan West Circuit chief controller Yan Li flattered Yan Zhen; when Zhen was ill he had him act as commissioner and in his final memorial recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Li fawned on Yan Zhen, acted during his illness, and was recommended in his final memorial.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，乙巳，以嚴礪為山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day yisi, Yan Li was made Shannan West Circuit military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on yisi, Yan Li was made military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙申，陳許節度使曲環薨。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day bingshen, Chen-Xu Military Commissioner Qu Huan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingshen, Qu Huan of Chen-Xu died.

sentences.zh: 乙未，吳少誠遣兵掠臨穎，陳州刺史上官涗知陳洲留後，遣大將王令忠將兵三千救之，皆為少誠所虜。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Wu Shaoqing sent troops to plunder Linying. Chenzhou Prefect Shangguan Shui, knowing Chenzhou affairs as acting commissioner, sent great general Wang Lingzhong with three thousand troops to rescue them—all were captured by Shaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing plundered Linying; Shangguan Shui's three thousand rescuers were captured.

sentences.zh: 九月，丙午，以涗為陳許節度使，少誠遂圍許州。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day bingwu, Shui was made Chen-Xu military commissioner; Shaoqing then besieged Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Shui was made Chen-Xu commissioner; Shaoqing besieged Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 涗欲棄城走，營田副使劉昌裔止之曰：「城中兵足以辦賊，但閉城勿與戰，不過數日，賊氣自衰，吾以全制其弊，蔑不克矣。」

translations.literal: Shui wished to abandon the city and flee; camp and field vice commissioner Liu Changyi stopped him, saying: "The troops in the city are enough to handle the bandits. Only close the city and do not fight; in no more than several days the bandits' spirit will decline of itself. I will overcome their weakness with our strength—we must prevail."
translations.idiomatic: “Shui meant to flee; Liu Changyi said closing the walls would break the besiegers' spirit.”

sentences.zh: 少誠晝夜急攻，昌裔募勇士千人鑿城出擊少誠，大破之，城由是全。

translations.literal: Shaoqing attacked day and night urgently. Changyi recruited a thousand brave men, broke out of the city, and struck Shaoqing, routing him greatly; the city was thereby preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi sallied with a thousand men and routed Shaoqing; the city was saved.

sentences.zh: 昌裔，兗州人也。

translations.literal: Changyi was a man of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi was from Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少誠又寇西華，陳許大將孟元陽拒卻之。

translations.literal: Shaoqing again raided Xihua; Chen-Xu great general Meng Yuanyang repelled him.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing raided Xihua; Meng Yuanyang repelled him.

sentences.zh: 陳許都知兵馬使安國寧與上官涗不葉，謀翻城應少誠，劉昌裔以計斬之。

translations.literal: Chen-Xu commander of all army horse affairs An Guoning was at odds with Shangguan Shui and plotted to turn the city to Shaoqing; Liu Changyi by stratagem beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: An Guoning plotted treason; Changyi executed him.

sentences.zh: 召其旄下，人給二縑。

translations.literal: He summoned his subordinates and gave each two bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Guoning's men and gave each two bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 伏兵要巷，見持縑者悉斬之，無得脫者。

translations.literal: Ambush troops waited in the lanes; all who held silk were cut down—none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Ambushers in the lanes killed every man holding silk.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，宣武節度使劉全諒薨。

translations.literal: On the day gengxu, Xuanwu Military Commissioner Liu Quanliang died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Liu Quanliang of Xuanwu died.

sentences.zh: 軍中思劉玄佐之恩，推其甥都知兵馬使匡城韓弘為留後。

translations.literal: The army remembered Liu Xuanzuo's kindness and pushed his nephew, commander of all army horse affairs Han Hong of Kuangcheng, as acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The army made Han Hong, Xuanzuo's nephew, acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 弘將兵，識其材鄙勇怯，指顧必堪其事。

translations.literal: When Hong led troops he knew each man's talent, vulgar courage or timidity; a glance showed who could handle the task.
translations.idiomatic: Hong knew every soldier's strengths at a glance.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詔削奪吳少誠官爵，令諸道進兵討之。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, an edict stripped Wu Shaoqing of office and enfeoffment and ordered all circuits to advance troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Shaoqing was stripped of rank and all circuits were ordered to attack him.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以韓弘為宣武節度使。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Han Hong was made Xuanwu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Han Hong was made Xuanwu military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 先是少慶遣使與劉全諒約共攻陳許，以陳州歸宣武。

translations.literal: Earlier Shaoqing had sent envoys to agree with Liu Quanliang to attack Chen-Xu jointly, giving Chenzhou to Xuanwu. Several envoys were still in the hostel; Hong drove them all out and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing's envoys to Quanliang were still in Bianzhou; Hong executed them.

sentences.zh: 使者數輩猶在館，弘悉驅出斬之。

translations.literal: He selected three thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He selected three thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 選卒三千。

translations.literal: They joined the various armies attacking Shaoqing below Xu.
translations.idiomatic: They joined the allied armies at Xu.

sentences.zh: 會諸軍擊少誠於許下。

translations.literal: Shaoqing thereby lost momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing lost momentum.

sentences.zh: 少誠由是失勢。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jichou, Prince Yuan of Yong died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, on jichou, Prince Yuan of Yong died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己丑，邕王源薨。

translations.literal: He was the heir apparent's son; the emperor loved and treated him as a son. When he died the posthumous title was Literary and Reverent Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's adopted son; he was posthumously titled Literary and Reverent Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 太子之子也，上愛而子之，及薨，謚曰文敬太子。

translations.literal: Shannan East Circuit Military Commissioner Yu Di, An-Huang Military Commissioner Yi Shen, and Wang Zong, who knew Shouzhou affairs, together with Shangguan Shui and Han Hong advanced against Wu Shaoqing and repeatedly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di, Yi Shen, Shui, and Hong repeatedly defeated Shaoqing.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使-{于}-頔、安黃節度使伊慎、知壽州事王宗與上官涗、韓弘進擊吳少誠，屢破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day renzi, Yu Di memorialized taking Wu Fang and Langshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renzi, Yu Di reported taking Wu Fang and Langshan.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬子，-{于}-頔奏拔吳房、朗山。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xinwei, Grand Preceptor and Prince Xianning Hun Jian died at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinwei, Hun Jian died at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛未，中書令、咸寧王渾瑊薨於河中。

translations.literal: Jian was modest and cautious by nature; though his rank reached general and chancellor he had no self-important air. Whenever he presented goods he always examined them in person; receiving gifts was as if before the emperor—therefore the emperor loved and cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian was humble despite his rank; the emperor loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 瑊性謙謹，雖位窮將相，無自矜大之色，每貢物必躬自閱視，受賜如在上前，由是為上所親愛。

translations.literal: After the emperor returned from Xingyuan, even where one prefecture or one command had troops, all were treated with indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingyuan the emperor indulged every garrison.

sentences.zh: 上還自興元，雖一州一鎮有兵者，皆務姑息。

translations.literal: Whenever Jian memorialized and was not approved he would privately rejoice, saying: "The emperor does not doubt me.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor rejected his advice, Jian rejoiced that he was still trusted.

sentences.zh: 瑊每奏事，不過，輒私喜曰：「上不疑我。」

translations.literal: Whenever Jian memorialized and was not approved he would privately rejoice, saying: "The emperor does not doubt me.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Hun Jian's memorials were rejected he would say privately, "The emperor still trusts me.

sentences.zh: 故能以功名終。

translations.literal: Six prefectures of Tangut since Yongtai had dwelt at Shizhou; Yong'an Fort commander Ashina Sijian encroached and harassed without end, and the Tangut tribes all fled west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Tangut tribes at Shizhou fled west under Ashina Sijian's oppression.

sentences.zh: 六州党項自永泰以來居於石州，永安鎮將阿史那思暕侵漁不已，党項部落悉逃奔河西。

translations.literal: The various armies attacking Wu Shaoqing had no overall commander; whenever they sent troops each man schemed for profit, and advance and retreat were not unified.
translations.idiomatic: The allied armies lacked a commander; each unit pursued its own gain.

sentences.zh: 諸軍討吳少誠者既無統帥，每出兵，人自規利，進退不壹。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei the various armies broke on their own at Xiao Yinshui, abandoning weapons and provisions and grain—all became Shaoqing's.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the allies collapsed at Xiao Yinshui and lost their supplies to Shaoqing.

sentences.zh: 乙未，諸軍自潰於小殷水，委棄器械、資糧，皆為少誠所有。

translations.literal: Thereupon they first discussed establishing a pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: They then decided to appoint a pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 於是始議置招討使。

translations.literal: Fifty thousand Tibetans divided to attack Nanzhao and Cizhou; Yimouxun and Wei Gao each sent troops to resist them; Tibet returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand Tibetans attacked Nanzhao and Cizhou; Yimouxun and Wei Gao drove them back.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃眾五萬分擊南詔及巂州，異牟尋與韋皋各發兵御之，吐蕃無功而還。

translations.literal: Fifty thousand Tibetans divided to attack Nanzhao and Cizhou; Yimouxun and Wei Gao each sent troops to resist them; Tibet returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand Tibetans attacked Nanzhao and Cizhou; Yimouxun and Wei Gao drove them back.

sentences.zh: 德宗神武聖文皇帝十貞元十六年（

translations.literal: Divine Martial and Sagacious Literary Emperor Dezong 10, sixteenth year of Zhenyuan (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, sixteenth year of Zhenyuan (

sentences.zh: 庚辰，公元八零零年）

translations.literal: gengchen, corresponding to AD 800)
translations.idiomatic: gengchen, AD 800)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙巳，恆冀、易定、陳許、河陽四軍與吳少誠戰，皆不利而退。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day yisi, the Heng-Ji, Yiding, Chen-Xu, and Heyang four armies fought Wu Shaoqing—all were unfavorable and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on yisi, four armies fought Shaoqing and were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 夏綏節度使韓全義本出神策軍，中尉竇文場愛厚之，薦於上，使統諸軍討吳少誠。

translations.literal: Xia-Sui Military Commissioner Han Quanyi was originally from the Shence Army; Chief Protector Dou Wenchang loved and favored him and recommended him to the emperor, making him command all armies to attack Wu Shaoqing.
translations.idiomatic: Han Quanyi of the Shence Army was Dou Wenchang's protégé and was put in command against Shaoqing.

sentences.zh: 二月乙酉，以全義為蔡州四面行營招討使，十七道兵皆受全義節度。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou in the second month, Quanyi was made pacification commissioner on all four sides of Caizhou; troops of seventeen circuits all received Quanyi's command.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou in the second month, Quanyi was made Caizhou pacification commissioner over seventeen circuits.

sentences.zh: 宣武軍自劉玄佐薨，凡五作亂，士卒益驕縱，輕其主帥。

translations.literal: Since Liu Xuanzuo's death the Xuanwu army had mutinied five times; the soldiers grew all the more arrogant and unrestrained and looked down on their commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xuanzuo's death Xuanwu had mutinied five times; the troops despised their commanders.

sentences.zh: 韓弘視事數月，皆知其主名，有郎將劉鍔，常為唱首。

translations.literal: Several months after Hong took office he knew the ringleaders by name; there was a commandant Liu E who often led the shouting.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Hong knew every ringleader; Liu E often led the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 三月，弘陳兵牙門，召鍔及其黨三百人，數之以：「數預於亂，自以為功」，悉斬之，血流丹道。

translations.literal: In the third month Hong arrayed troops at the headquarters gate, summoned E and his faction of three hundred, and counted their crimes: "You have repeatedly joined in disorder and consider it merit"—and beheaded them all; blood flowed on the red avenue.
translations.idiomatic: “In the third month Hong executed Liu E and three hundred mutineers at headquarters; blood ran in the street.”

sentences.zh: 自是至弘入朝二十一年，士卒無一人敢歡呼於城郭者。

translations.literal: From this until Hong entered court twenty-one years later, not one soldier dared shout in the streets.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty-one years until Hong went to court, no soldier dared riot in the streets.

sentences.zh: 義成監軍薛盈珍為上所寵信，欲奪節度使姚南仲軍政，南仲不從，由是有隙。

translations.literal: Yicheng army supervisor Xue Yingzhen was favored and trusted by the emperor and wished to seize military government from Military Commissioner Yao Nanzhong; Nanzhong would not agree, and therefore there was a rift.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yingzhen tried to seize Yao Nanzhong's command; Nanzhong refused.

sentences.zh: 盈珍譖其幕僚□，貶泉州別駕。

translations.literal: Yingzhen slandered his staff member and had him demoted to vice prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen slandered a staff member into exile at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使柳冕謀害總以媚盈珍，遣幕僚寶鼎薛戎攝泉州事，使按致總罪，戎為辯證其無辜。

translations.literal: Fujian Observation Commissioner Liu Mian plotted to harm the man to please Yingzhen and sent staff member Baoding Xue Rong to act as Quanzhou affairs; he was to investigate and establish the man's crimes. Rong argued to prove his innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian of Fujian tried to kill the man for Yingzhen; Xue Rong defended his innocence.

sentences.zh: 冕怒，召戎，囚之，使守卒恣為侵辱。

translations.literal: Mian was angry, summoned Rong, imprisoned him, and had the guards freely insult and humiliate him.
translations.idiomatic: Mian imprisoned Rong and had guards abuse him.

sentences.zh: 如此累月，徐誘之使誣總，戎終不從，總由是獲免。

translations.literal: For months thus he gradually induced him to frame the man; Rong in the end would not agree, and the man thereby escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: For months Mian tried to make Rong frame the man; Rong refused and the man was spared.

sentences.zh: 冕，芳之子也。

translations.literal: Mian was the son of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was Fang's son.

sentences.zh: 盈珍屢毀南仲於上，上疑之。

translations.literal: Yingzhen repeatedly slandered Nanzhong to the emperor; the emperor grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen slandered Nanzhong until the emperor doubted him.

sentences.zh: 盈珍又遣小吏程務盈乘驛誣奏南仲罪。

translations.literal: Yingzhen also sent a petty clerk Cheng Wuying by post horse to lodge a false memorial of Nanzhong's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen sent Cheng Wuying to accuse Nanzhong falsely.

sentences.zh: 牙將曹文洽亦奏事長安，知之，晨夜兼行，追及務盈於長樂驛，與之同宿，中夜，殺之，沉盈珍表於廁中。

translations.literal: Adjutant Cao Wenzhi also memorialized at Chang'an; knowing this, he traveled day and night, overtook Wuying at Changle Post, lodged with him, and at midnight killed him and sank Yingzhen's memorial in the privy.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wenzhi overtook Wuying at Changle Post, killed him, and destroyed Yingzhen's memorial.

sentences.zh: 自作表雪南仲之冤，且首專殺之罪，亦作狀白南仲，遂自殺。

translations.literal: He himself made a memorial clearing Nanzhong's wrong and also confessing the crime of unauthorized killing, and made a statement informing Nanzhong, then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a memorial clearing Nanzhong, confessed to murder, informed Nanzhong, and killed himself.

sentences.zh: 明旦，門不啟，驛吏排之入，得表、狀於文洽屍旁。

translations.literal: At dawn the gate did not open; the post clerks broke in and found the memorial and statement beside Wenzhi's corpse.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the post station found his body and the memorials.

sentences.zh: 上聞而異之，征盈珍入朝。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he marveled and summoned Yingzhen to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marveled and summoned Yingzhen to court.

sentences.zh: 南仲恐盈珍讒之益深，亦請入朝。

translations.literal: Nanzhong feared Yingzhen's slanders would deepen and also asked to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong also came to court for fear of Yingzhen.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丙子，南仲至京師，待罪於金吾。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day bingzi, Nanzhong reached the capital and awaited punishment at the Jinwu guard.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on bingzi, Nanzhong reached the capital to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 詔釋之，召見。

translations.literal: An edict released him and he was summoned to audience.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned him and he was received in audience.

sentences.zh: 上問：「盈珍擾卿邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "Did Yingzhen harass you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Did Yingzhen harass you?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「盈珍不擾臣，但亂陛下法耳。

translations.literal: He replied: "Yingzhen did not harass your servant—he only disturbed Your Majesty's laws.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Yingzhen did not harass me—he disturbed Your Majesty's laws.

sentences.zh: 且天下如盈珍輩，何可勝數！

translations.literal: Moreover, throughout the realm men like Yingzhen—how can they be numbered!
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yingzhen are beyond counting."

sentences.zh: 雖使羊、杜復生，亦不能行愷悌之政，成攻取之功也。」

translations.literal: Even if Yang Xiu and Du Yu were reborn they could not carry out benevolent government or achieve merit in attack."
translations.idiomatic: Not even Yang Xiu and Du Yu reborn could govern benevolently or win battles.

sentences.zh: 上默然，竟不罪盈珍，仍使掌機密。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent and in the end did not punish Yingzhen, still having him manage confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent and kept Yingzhen in power.

sentences.zh: 盈珍又言於上曰：「南仲惡政，皆幕僚馬少微贊之也。」

translations.literal: Yingzhen again spoke to the emperor, saying: "Nanzhong's evil government was all urged by his staff member Ma Shaowei."
translations.idiomatic: “Yingzhen claimed Nanzhong's abuses were Ma Shaowei's doing.”

sentences.zh: 詔貶少微江南官，遣中使送之，推墜江中而死。

translations.literal: An edict demoted Shaowei to an office south of the Yangzi and sent a palace envoy to escort him; he was pushed into the river and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowei was demoted and drowned en route by the envoy.

sentences.zh: 黔中觀察使韋士宗，政令苛刻。

translations.literal: Qianzhong Observation Commissioner Wei Shizong's government orders were harsh and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shizong of Qianzhong ruled harshly.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，牙將傅近等逐之，出奔施州。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai, adjutant Fu Jin and others expelled him; he fled to Shi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Fu Jin expelled him to Shi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 新羅王敬則卒，庚寅，冊命其嫡孫俊邕為新羅王。

translations.literal: Silla King Gyeongjeon died. On the day gengyin, his eldest grandson Junyeong was invested as king of Silla.
translations.idiomatic: Silla's Gyeongjeon died; on gengyin Junyeong was invested king.

sentences.zh: 韓全義素無勇略，專以巧佞貨賂結宦官得為大帥，每議軍事，宦官為監軍者數十人坐帳中爭論，紛然莫能決而罷。

translations.literal: Han Quanyi had never had courage or strategy; he relied solely on flattery and bribes to eunuchs to become a great commander. Whenever military affairs were discussed, several dozen eunuchs as army supervisors sat in the tent arguing; in confusion nothing could be decided and they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi lacked courage and let eunuch supervisors argue in his tent.

sentences.zh: 天漸暑，士卒久屯沮洳之地，多病疫，全義不存撫，人有離心。

translations.literal: Heaven gradually grew hot; the soldiers long encamped in damp low ground and many fell ill with plague. Quanyi did not care for them and men had hearts to leave.
translations.idiomatic: In summer heat and plague, Quanyi neglected his troops.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚戌，與吳少誠將吳秀、吳少陽等戰於殷南廣利原，鋒鏑未交，諸軍大潰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day gengxu, he fought Wu Shaoqing's generals Wu Xiu and Wu Shaoyang and others at Guangli Plain south of Yin; before blades crossed the various armies broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu at Guangli Plain the allies routed before battle was joined.

sentences.zh: 秀等乘之，全義退保五樓。

translations.literal: Xiu and others pressed them; Quanyi withdrew to defend Wulou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu pursued; Quanyi fled to Wulou.

sentences.zh: 少陽，滄州清池人也。

translations.literal: Shaoyang was a man of Qingchi in Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyang was from Qingchi in Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使-{于}-頔因討吳少誠，大募戰士，繕甲厲兵，聚斂貨財，恣行誅殺，有據漢南之志，專以慢上陵下為事。

translations.literal: Shannan East Circuit Military Commissioner Yu Di, because he was attacking Wu Shaoqing, greatly recruited warriors, repaired armor and sharpened weapons, amassed wealth, and executed at will, harboring ambition to hold the Han south and making slighting the emperor and bullying subordinates his business.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di built power attacking Shaoqing and defied the throne.

sentences.zh: 上方姑息籓鎮，知其所為，無如之何。

translations.literal: The emperor was then indulging the frontier commands and knew what he did but could do nothing about it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor indulged him helplessly.

sentences.zh: 頔誣鄧州刺史元洪贓罪，朝廷不得已流洪端州，遣中使護送至棗陽。

translations.literal: Di falsely charged Dengzhou Prefect Yuan Hong with embezzlement; the court had no choice but to exile Hong to Duanzhou and sent a palace envoy to escort him to Zaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Di framed Yuan Hong; the court exiled him to Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 頔遣兵劫取歸襄州，中使奔歸。

translations.literal: Di sent troops to intercept and take him back to Xiangzhou; the palace envoy fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Di's troops seized Hong; the envoy fled.

sentences.zh: 頔表洪責太重，上復以洪為吉州長史，乃遣之。

translations.literal: Di memorialized that Hong's punishment was too heavy; the emperor again made Hong chief administrator of Jizhou and then sent him on.
translations.idiomatic: The court relented and made Hong chief administrator of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 又怒判官薛正倫，奏貶峽州長史。

translations.literal: He was also angry with judge Xue Zhenglun and memorialized demoting him to chief administrator of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also demoted judge Xue Zhenglun.

sentences.zh: 比敕下，頔怒已解，復奏留為判官。

translations.literal: By the time the edict descended Di's anger had eased and he again memorialized to keep him as judge.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived Di had cooled and kept Zhenglun as judge.

sentences.zh: 上一一從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed each in turn.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed to each request.

sentences.zh: 徐、泗、濠節度使張建封鎮彭城十餘年，軍府稱治，病篤，累表請除代人。

translations.literal: Xu, Si, and Hao Military Commissioner Zhang Jianfeng had governed Pengcheng more than ten years; the military headquarters was called well ordered. Critically ill, he repeatedly memorialized requesting a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jianfeng, ill after ten years at Xuzhou, asked for a successor.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以蘇州刺史夏卿為徐、泗、濠行軍司馬。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, Suzhou Prefect Xia Qing was made Xu, Si, and Hao campaigning army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Xia Qing was made campaigning marshal of Xu, Si, and Hao.

sentences.zh: 敕下，建封已薨。

translations.literal: When the edict descended Jianfeng had already died.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict arrived Jianfeng was dead.

sentences.zh: 夏卿，執誼之從祖兄也。

translations.literal: Xia Qing was a cousin of Zhiyi on the father's line.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Qing was Wei Zhiyi's cousin.

sentences.zh: 徐州判官鄭通誠知留後，恐軍士為變，會浙西兵過彭城，通誠欲引入城為援。

translations.literal: Xuzhou judge Zheng Tongcheng knew remaining affairs and feared the soldiers would mutiny. When Zhexi troops passed Pengcheng, Tongcheng wished to lead them into the city as support.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Zheng Tongcheng tried to bring Zhexi troops into Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 軍士怒，壬子，數千人斧庫門，出甲兵擐執之，圍牙城，劫建封子前虢州參軍愔令知軍府事，殺通誠及大將段伯熊等數人，械系監軍。

translations.literal: The soldiers were angry. On the day renzi several thousand men axed the armory gate, took out armor and weapons and donned them, surrounded the headquarters, forced Jianfeng's son former Guozhou staff officer Yin to take military headquarters affairs, killed Tongcheng and great general Duan Boxiong and several others, and chained the army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the troops mutinied, made Yin commander, and killed Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，以吏部員外郎李鄘為徐州宣慰使。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he made Ministry of Personnel vice director Li Yun Xuzhou comforting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Li Yun as comforting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鄘直抵其軍，召將士宣朝旨，諭以禍福，脫監軍械，使復其位，凶黨不敢犯。

translations.literal: Yun went straight to the army, summoned officers and soldiers, proclaimed the court's intent, explained fortune and misfortune, removed the army supervisor's chains and restored his position; the violent faction did not dare offend.
translations.idiomatic: Yun restored order and freed the army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 愔上表稱兵馬留後，鄘以非朝命，不受，使削去，然後受之以歸。

translations.literal: Yin submitted a memorial claiming army horse acting commissioner; Yun, because it was not a court order, would not accept it and had him strike it out before accepting and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Yin claimed acting command; Yun refused until the illegal title was removed.

sentences.zh: 靈州破吐蕃於烏蘭橋。

translations.literal: Lingzhou defeated Tibet at Wulan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Lingzhou defeated Tibet at Wulan Bridge.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，韋士宗復入黔中。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Wei Shizong re-entered Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Wei Shizong returned to Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 湖南觀察使河中呂渭奏發永州刺史陽履贓賄，履表稱所斂物皆備進奉。

translations.literal: Hunan Observation Commissioner Hezhong Lü Wei memorialized exposing Yongzhou Prefect Yang Lü's embezzlement; Lü memorialized that what he collected was all prepared for presentation tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Wei accused Yang Lü of embezzlement; Lü claimed it was tribute.

sentences.zh: 上召詣長安，丁丑，命三司使鞫之，詰其物費用所歸，履對曰：「已市馬進之矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him to Chang'an. On the day dingchou he ordered the three offices to interrogate him and pressed where the goods' expenses went. Lü replied: "I have already bought horses and presented them."
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an, Lü was interrogated about the funds; he said he had bought horses for tribute."

sentences.zh: 又詰：「馬主為誰？

translations.literal: They pressed again: "Who is the horse owner?
translations.idiomatic: “They asked who owned the horses.

sentences.zh: 馬齒幾何？」

translations.literal: How many teeth does the horse have?"
translations.idiomatic: How old were they?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「馬主，東西南北之人，今不知所之。

translations.literal: He replied: "The horse owner is a man from east, west, south, or north—now I do not know where he has gone.
translations.idiomatic: “He said the owners were from everywhere and could not be found."

sentences.zh: 按《禮》，齒路馬有誅，故不知其齒。」

translations.literal: According to the Rites, road horses past their prime are executed—therefore I do not know their teeth."
translations.idiomatic: By the Rites, worn-out road horses are destroyed—so I do not know their age.

sentences.zh: 所對率類此。

translations.literal: His answers were mostly of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His answers were all evasions.

sentences.zh: 上悅其進奉之言，釋之，但免官而已。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased with his presentation-tribute talk, released him, and only removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was amused and only removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，加淄青節度使李師古同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu, Zi-Qing Military Commissioner Li Shigu was made fellow grand councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Li Shigu was made fellow grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 徐州亂兵為張愔表求旄節，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: The Xuzhou mutineers memorialized for Zhang Yin requesting a command baton; the court did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou mutineers asked for a commission for Yin; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 加淮南節度使杜佑同平章事，兼徐、濠、泗節度使，使討之。

translations.literal: Huainan Military Commissioner Du You was made fellow grand councillor and concurrent Xu, Hao, and Si military commissioner to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Du You was made fellow councillor and ordered to attack Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 佑大具舟艦，遣牙將孟准為前鋒。

translations.literal: You greatly prepared boats and ships and sent adjutant Meng Zhun as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: You sent Meng Zhun as naval vanguard.

sentences.zh: 濟淮而敗，佑不敢進。

translations.literal: Crossing the Huai he was defeated; You dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhun was beaten crossing the Huai; You halted.

sentences.zh: 泗州刺史張伾出兵攻橋伾，大敗而還。

translations.literal: Si Prefecture Prefect Zhang Yi sent troops to attack Qiaoyi and was greatly defeated in returning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yi attacked Qiaoyi and was routed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷不得已除愔徐州團練使，以伾為泗州留後，濠州刺史杜兼為濠州留後，仍加佑兼濠泗觀察使。

translations.literal: The court had no choice but to appoint Yin Xuzhou training commissioner, make Yi Si Prefecture acting commissioner, and Hao Prefect Du Jian Hao Prefecture acting commissioner, still adding You as concurrent Hao-Si observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Yin training commissioner and Yi and Du acting commissioners.

sentences.zh: 兼，正倫五世孫也，性狡險強忍。

translations.literal: Jian was Zhenglun's fifth-generation descendant and was by nature crafty, dangerous, and forcibly enduring.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jian was crafty and ruthless.

sentences.zh: 建封之疾亟也，兼陰圖代之，自濠州疾驅至府。

translations.literal: When Jianfeng's illness was critical Jian secretly plotted to replace him and galloped from Hao Prefecture to the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: As Jianfeng lay dying Du Jian raced from Hao to seize power.

sentences.zh: 幕僚李籓與同列，入問建封疾，出見之，泣曰：「僕射疾危如此，公宜在州防遏，今棄州此來，欲何為也！

translations.literal: Staff member Li Fan and his colleagues entered to inquire after Jianfeng's illness; coming out they saw Jian and wept, saying: "The prefect's illness is so critical—sir ought to stay at the prefecture to guard against trouble. Now you abandon the prefecture and come here—what do you intend!
translations.idiomatic: “Li Fan drove Du Jian away from the dying Jianfeng's bedside.

sentences.zh: 宜速去，不然，當奏之。」

translations.literal: You should leave quickly; otherwise I shall memorialize."
translations.idiomatic: Leave at once or I will report you."

sentences.zh: 兼錯愕出不意，遂徑歸。

translations.literal: Jian was startled beyond expectation and went straight back.
translations.idiomatic: Jian fled back to Hao.

sentences.zh: 建封薨，籓歸揚州，兼誣奏籓於建封之薨搖動軍情，上大怒，密詔杜佑使殺之。

translations.literal: When Jianfeng died Fan returned to Yangzhou; Jian falsely memorialized that Fan, at Jianfeng's death, had shaken army sentiment. The emperor was greatly angered and secretly ordered Du You to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian slandered Fan; the emperor secretly ordered You to kill him.

sentences.zh: 佑素重籓，懷詔旬日不忍發，因引籓論佛經曰，「佛言果報，有諸？」

translations.literal: You had always valued Fan and held the secret edict ten days without daring send it. He therefore drew Fan into discussing Buddhism, saying: "The Buddha speaks of karmic retribution—is there such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: You delayed the edict and tested Fan with talk of karma."

sentences.zh: 籓曰：「有之」。

translations.literal: Fan said: "There is."
translations.idiomatic: “Fan said there was.”

sentences.zh: 佑曰：「審如此，君宜遇事無恐。」

translations.literal: You said: "If it is truly so, you ought to meet affairs without fear."
translations.idiomatic: You told him not to fear."

sentences.zh: 因出詔示籓。

translations.literal: He then produced the edict and showed Fan.
translations.idiomatic: He showed Fan the edict.

sentences.zh: 籓神色不變，曰：「此真報也。」

translations.literal: Fan's expression did not change. He said: "This is true retribution."
translations.idiomatic: Fan said calmly, "This is retribution."

sentences.zh: 佑曰：「君慎勿出口，吾已密論，用百口保君矣。」

translations.literal: You said: "Be careful not to let it out—I have already argued secretly and guarantee you with a hundred mouths."
translations.idiomatic: “You promised to save him with a hundred lives.”

sentences.zh: 上猶疑之，召籓詣長安，望見籓儀度安雅，乃曰：』此豈為惡者邪！

translations.literal: The emperor still doubted and summoned Fan to Chang'an. Seeing Fan's bearing calm and elegant he said: "How could this be an evil man!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw Fan's calm bearing and spared him.

sentences.zh: 即除秘書郎。

translations.literal: He at once made him secretary gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He made Fan a secretary.

sentences.zh: 新羅王俊邕卒，國人立其子重熙。

translations.literal: Silla's Junyeong died; the people installed his son Chongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Junyeong of Silla died; Chongxi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，吳少誠進擊韓全義於五樓，諸軍復大敗。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Wu Shaoqing advanced to attack Han Quanyi at Wulou; the various armies were again greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Shaoqing attacked Quanyi at Wulou and routed the allies again.

sentences.zh: 全義夜遁，保殷水縣城。

translations.literal: Quanyi fled by night and defended Yingshui county city.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi fled by night to Yingshui.

sentences.zh: 盧龍節度使劉濟弟源為涿州刺史，不受濟命；

translations.literal: Lulong Military Commissioner Liu Ji's younger brother Yuan was Zhuozhou prefect and would not obey Ji's order;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji's brother Yuan, prefect of Zhuo, defied him;

sentences.zh: 濟引兵擊擒之。

translations.literal: Ji led troops, attacked, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji captured him by force.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸卯，義成節度使盧群薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day guimao, Yicheng Military Commissioner Lu Qun died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guimao, Lu Qun of Yicheng died.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，以尚書左丞李元素代之。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Yuansu was made to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Li Yuansu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 賈耽曰：「凡就軍中除節度使，必有愛憎向背，喜懼者相半，故眾心多不安。

translations.literal: Jia Dan said: "Whenever one is appointed military commissioner from within the army there must be likes, dislikes, favor, and fear—half rejoice and half fear—so the army's heart is mostly unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: “Jia Dan urged appointing commissioners from court, not from the army."

sentences.zh: 自今願陛下只自朝廷除人，庶無它變。」

translations.literal: From now on I wish Your Majesty would appoint men only from the court—then there will be no other changes."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint only from the capital and there will be no turmoil.

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事鄭餘慶與戶部侍郎、判度支于(

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow Grand Councillor Zheng Yuqing was on good terms with Vice Minister of Revenue and Commissioner of Public Revenue Yu Pi;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing was close to Yu Pi of the Revenue Ministry;

sentences.zh: 丕頁)

translations.literal: Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Pi)

sentences.zh: 善，所奏事，餘慶多勸上從之。

translations.literal: Whatever they memorialized, Yuqing mostly urged the emperor to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing usually urged the emperor to follow Pi's advice.

sentences.zh: 上以為朋比，庚戌，貶餘慶郴州司馬，(

translations.literal: The emperor thought this factional collusion. On the day gengxu he demoted Yuqing to militia officer of Chenzhou and (
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw factionalism. On gengxu he demoted Yuqing to Chenzhou and (

sentences.zh: 丕頁)

translations.literal: Yu Pi)
translations.idiomatic: Yu Pi)

sentences.zh: 泉州司戶。

translations.literal: Quanzhou registrar.
translations.idiomatic: registrar of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: (丕頁)，

translations.literal: Pi),
translations.idiomatic: Pi),

sentences.zh: 頔之兄也。

translations.literal: elder brother of Di.
translations.idiomatic: elder brother of Yu Di.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，吳少誠進逼殷水數里置營，韓全義復帥諸軍退保陳州。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Wu Shaoqing advanced and pressed within several li of Yinshui and set camp; Han Quanyi again led the various armies to withdraw and defend Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Shaoqing camped near Yinshui; Quanyi retreated to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣武、河陽兵私歸本道，獨陳許將孟元陽、神策將蘇光榮所部留軍殷水。

translations.literal: Xuanwu and Heyang troops privately returned to their circuits; only Chen-Xu general Meng Yuanyang and Shence general Su Guangrong detachments remained encamped at Yinshui.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanwu and Heyang troops went home; only Yuanyang and Guangrong stayed at Yinshui.

sentences.zh: 全義以詐誘昭義將夏侯仲宣、義成將時昂、河陽將權文變、河中將郭湘等，斬之，欲以威眾。

translations.literal: Quanyi by deception lured Zhaoyi general Xiahou Zhongxuan, Yicheng general Shi Ang, Heyang general Quan Wenbian, and Hezhong general Guo Xiang and others, beheaded them, wishing to awe the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi lured and executed Zhongxuan, Ang, Wenbian, and Xiang to intimidate the army.

sentences.zh: 全義至陳州，刺史劉昌裔登城謂之曰：「天子命公討蔡州，今乃來此，昌裔不敢納，請捨於城外。」

translations.literal: When Quanyi reached Chenzhou, Prefect Liu Changyi mounted the wall and said to him: "The Son of Heaven ordered you, sir, to attack Caizhou—now you come here. Changyi dare not admit you; please encamp outside the city."
translations.idiomatic: “At Chenzhou, Liu Changyi refused Quanyi entry and told him to camp outside.”

sentences.zh: 既而昌裔繼牛酒入全義營犒師，全義驚喜，心服之。

translations.literal: Soon after Changyi followed with cattle and wine into Quanyi camp to reward the army; Quanyi was startled and pleased and submitted in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Changyi then feasted the army; Quanyi was won over.

sentences.zh: 己未，孟元陽等與少誠戰，殺二千餘人。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, Meng Yuanyang and others fought Shaoqing and killed more than two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, Yuanyang killed more than two thousand of Shaoqing men.

sentences.zh: 庚申，以太常卿齊抗為中書舍人、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, Court of Imperial Sacrifices director Qi Kang was made drafting secretary and fellow grand councillor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, Qi Kang was made fellow grand councillor.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以張愔為徐州留後。

translations.literal: On the day guihai, Zhang Yin was made Xuzhou acting commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, Zhang Yin was made acting commissioner of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，吳少誠引兵還蔡州。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Wu Shaoqing led troops back to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Shaoqing withdrew to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，韋皋聞諸軍討少誠無功，上言「請以渾瑊、賈耽為元帥，統諸軍。

translations.literal: Earlier Wei Gao, hearing the various armies had attacked Shaoqing without success, memorialized: "I ask that Hun Jian and Jia Dan be made supreme commanders to command all armies.
translations.idiomatic: “Wei Gao proposed Hun Jian and Jia Dan as supreme commanders.

sentences.zh: 若重煩元老，則臣請以精銳萬人下巴峽，出荊楚以翦凶逆。

translations.literal: If the court is unwilling to trouble elder statesmen, then your servant asks to lead ten thousand elite troops down the Ba Gorge, emerge in Jing-Chu, and cut down the villain.
translations.idiomatic: Or he offered ten thousand men through the Ba Gorge into Jing-Chu.

sentences.zh: 不然，因其請罪而赦之，罷兩河諸軍以休息私公，亦策之次也。

translations.literal: Otherwise, because he pleads guilt, pardon him and dismiss the Hebei armies to rest both public and private—that too is a secondary strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Or pardon Shaoqing and disband the armies—that was his second choice.

sentences.zh: 若少誠一旦罪盈惡稔，為麾下所殺，則又當以其爵位授之，是除一少誠，生一少誠，為患無窮矣。」

translations.literal: If Shaoqing one day overflows with crimes and is killed by his subordinates, then you will again have to give his rank and title to the successor—is removing one Shaoqing and begetting one Shaoqing, harm without end."
translations.idiomatic: Kill one Shaoqing and another rises—endless trouble."

sentences.zh: 賈耽言於上曰：「賊意蓋亦望恩貸，恐須開其生路。」

translations.literal: Jia Dan spoke to the emperor, saying: "The bandit intent surely also hopes for grace and pardon—we probably must open a path for his life."
translations.idiomatic: “Jia Dan urged opening a path to mercy.”

sentences.zh: 上然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 會少誠致書幣於監官軍者求昭洗，監軍奏之。

translations.literal: It happened that Shaoqing sent letters and gifts to the army supervisors asking to clear his name; the supervisors memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoqing asked for amnesty through the army supervisors.

sentences.zh: 戊子，詔赦少誠及彰義將士，復其官爵。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, an edict pardoned Shaoqing and Zhangyi officers and soldiers and restored their offices and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Shaoqing and the Zhangyi army were pardoned and restored.

sentences.zh: 己丑，河東節度使李說薨。

translations.literal: On the day jichou, Hedong Military Commissioner Li Shuo died.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Li Shuo of Hedong died.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以其行軍司馬鄭儋為節度使。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, his campaigning army marshal Zheng Dan was made military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Zheng Dan was made military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上擇可以代儋者，以刑部員外郎嚴綬嘗以幕僚進奉，記其名，即用為河東行軍司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor chose someone who could replace Dan; because Ministry of Justice vice director Yan Shou had once presented tribute as a staff member, he noted his name and at once made him Hedong campaigning army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shou, remembered for tribute as a staffer, was made Hedong campaigning marshal.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃數為韋皋所敗，同歲，其曩貢、臘城等九節度嬰、籠官馬定德帥其部落來降。

translations.literal: Tibet was repeatedly defeated by Wei Gao; the same year, infant and cage officials Ma Dingde of the nine prefectures Nangong, Lacheng, and others led their tribes to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet suffered repeated defeats; Ma Dingde and others surrendered.

sentences.zh: 定德有智略，吐蕃諸將行兵，皆稟其謀策，常乘驛計事，至是以兵數不利，恐獲罪，遂來奔。

translations.literal: Dingde had strategy; whenever Tibetan generals marched they all received his plans. He often rode post horses to calculate affairs; because troop numbers were now unfavorable and he feared punishment, he therefore came to defect.
translations.idiomatic: Dingde had advised Tibetan campaigns; fearing blame, he defected.
